Findings:

- **No admin-only capability is reachable by a plain user** — every `/admin/...` mutating route carries `RequireAdmin` with a per-request DB check. The one exception by design is `GET /api/v1/admin/me` (any authed user; naming only).
- **No route is fully unguarded except the intended three**: register, login, health, provider webhooks. (Order endpoints require API keys.)
- **The partition violation is the opposite direction**: there is no customer-only guard. An admin session token is accepted on every merchant/org route, and every session token (admin or not) is accepted on `RequireAuth`-only routes. There is no audience to reject cross-use. `MerchantRoute.tsx:6-8` even documents "admins included" as intentional.
- Merchant withdrawal approve/reject (`app.go:202-203`) is dual-homed: finance/owner org members **and** (separately) admins via the `/admin/withdrawals` routes — legitimate overlap to preserve, not a bug.

### 3. Data model

- `app.organizations` + `app.org_members(owner|finance|developer|viewer, invited|active)` (`000035_organizations.up.sql:7-39`). Permission matrix single-sourced in `backend/internal/modules/orgs/model.go:44-57` (`Can`). Server-side role resolution everywhere; client-supplied roles validated via `ParseRole` (`model.go:60-67`).
- `payment_apps.org_id NOT NULL` (`000037_apps_org_not_null`); legacy `payment_app_members` left untouched (`000024`, `000036` backfill doc). `org_members.user_id` is **UUID with no FK to `app.users`** (`000035:29`) — orphan risk if users are deleted.
- API keys: `app.payment_api_keys` with `environment live|sandbox` (`000034`, `000040`); orders carry `environment` from the **key, never the body** (`payments/handler.go:267-279`). Live gate `requireLiveKYC` (`handler.go:213-233`) + merchant key-create/rotate gates (`:1706-1709`, `:1734-1736`) return `403 kyc_required` — service/handler layer, as the goal wants. Sandbox provider guard exists too.
- KYC: `app.kyc_submissions` one-row-per-org + `organizations.kyc_status pending|submitted|verified|rejected` (`000039`, `000035:12-13`). Submit/resubmit clears review fields; only `submitted` is decidable (`409 not_in_review`, `orgs/handler.go:506-515`); reject requires reason (validated, `orgs/service.go` + `handler.go:483-504` — I read the handler; service mirrors it with tests in `kyc_test.go`).
- Ledger/withdrawals/webhooks: standard tables (`000023`, `000026`, `000008`, `000027`, `000031`); balances per-currency; idempotency keys (`000033`); refunds (`000031`).
- Introducing `org_id` ownership is **already done** (apps → orgs → members). Nothing to backfill except the already-handled legacy `payment_app_members`.
- **Missing vs. goal §Phase 2/3**: no `suspend/unsuspend` columns on orgs/apps; no per-org **fee** override (only per-app fees + per-org **live limits** `000043_org_live_limits`); `kyc_submissions` lacks `reviewed_by/rejected` actor FK shape goal wants (`reviewed_by TEXT` email only) and has no status column of its own (status lives on `organizations`); **no `audit_log` table at all** (see §5).

### 4. Frontend inventory (`frontend/src/`)

- Single React app, single router (`App.tsx:1-97`), single token key, single layout `pages/AdminLayout.tsx:1-108` used for **both** admin and merchant routes (nav mixes Overview/Apps/Withdrawals/Providers + Merchant + conditional KYC-review, `:9-19,36`). No visual admin/customer distinction, org switcher shown to admins too.
- API clients: `lib/auth.ts` (token + login/register), `lib/adminApi.ts` (all `/admin/...` + `getAdminMe`), `lib/merchantApi.ts` (`/merchant/...`), `lib/orgApi.ts` (`/orgs/...` + admin KYC-queue helpers `:186-205` — **admin calls share the customer token client**), `lib/signupApi.ts` (OTP + customer KYC upload, but `getMe()` hits `/api/v1/admin/me` `:86-88`).
- Guards: `components/AdminRoute.tsx` (allows iff `getAdminMe().is_admin`, else "Not an admin" message `:42-58`) and `components/MerchantRoute.tsx` (allows **any** signed-in user, admins included `:6-8`). Both redirect to single `/signin`.
- Pages: `SignIn` (combined login/register toggle, `SignIn.tsx:18-29`), `SignUp` (email+OTP), `AdminPayments`, `AdminPaymentApps`, `AdminPaymentAppDetail`, `AdminPaymentWithdrawals`, `AdminPaymentProviders`, `AdminKYCReview` (admin-flavored); `MerchantApps`, `MerchantAppDetail`, `CreateOrg`, `OrgMembers`, `OrgSettings`, `OnboardingKYC` (customer-flavored). No `/login`, `/register`, `/verify-email`, `/dashboard`, `/admin/login`, org-apps/detail/keys/webhooks/deliveries pages as separate customer routes (merchant detail page covers them in tabs — verify before splitting), no audit-log viewer, no `404` (wildcard redirects to `/admin/payments`, `App.tsx:89-90` — leaks admin path to customers).
- `SandboxModeBanner.tsx:1-43` already implements the unverified-org banner with KYC link. No sandbox/live badge or org switcher split yet.

### 5. KYC / OTP / mailer / SMS / upload / audit / notify

| Capability | State |
|---|---|
| OTP email+SMS | **Built** (`auth.go:340-494`): 6-digit crypto-rand, bcrypt hash, 10-min TTL, 5/hr rate limit, 5-attempt lockout, TZ phone validation. Tests in `otp_test.go`. |
| Mailer/SMS | **Log-only stubs that SUCCEED** (`auth.go:506-533`, wired `app.go:57-58`). `LogMailer.SendEmail`/`LogSMSSender.SendSMS` return `nil`. The backend README's claim of `503 otp_not_configured` is **stale** — with the current wiring OTP "sends" always succeed and codes must be read from `app.otp_codes` in dev. No SES/SendGrid/Beem wired. |
| KYC submit/status/resubmit + queue + approve/reject + limits | **Built** both sides (`orgs/handler.go:316-569`, `AdminKYCReview.tsx`, `OnboardingKYC.tsx`). Rejection reason required; resubmit allowed. |
| Document upload | **Built**: JPEG/PNG/WEBP/PDF, content-sniff + extension check, 5 MB cap, `backend/uploads/kyc/` with `0750/0640` perms, `orgID-nano` filenames, served only via authed endpoints with `..` confinement (`orgs/handler.go:287-308, 355-440, 548-569`). Local disk only; no S3, no virus scan, `uploads/` is git-untracked working dir. |
| Audit log | **Interface only, never wired, no table**: `shared/audit/audit.go` (`LogAdminAction`) and `shared/notify/notify.go` (`CreateAdminNotification`) exist; `app.go:88-92` explicitly notes nothing is wired and calls no-op. No `audit_log` migration. **No admin mutation writes an audit row today.** |
| Notifications on approve/reject | **None** — review path records reviewer email only. |
| Login rate limit / lockout / 2FA | **None** on `/auth/login` (only OTP request has rate limiting). `login_2fa` OTP purpose is defined but unused. No failed-login audit. |
| Email-verification gate | **Not enforced backend-side** — dashboard/org access works unverified; only the frontend signup flow nudges verification. |

### 6. Risks making the partition unsafe today

1. **One token fits everywhere**: same secret, same claims, same TTL, no audience. Cross-use is accepted by design, not rejected with 401/403.
2. **`is_admin` in JWT** (`auth.go:27-33,67`): currently unread for auth decisions, but its presence invites future `claims.IsAdmin` shortcuts that would reintroduce stale-privilege bugs.
3. **Shared middleware chain + `/admin/me` under the admin prefix without `RequireAdmin`**: confusing but not exploitable; rename/relocate matters for the "clear JSON error on wrong audience" goal.
4. **Single localStorage token** across admin+customer clients: XSS steals both personas at once; no `httpOnly` cookie option, no separate storage keys, no separate lifetimes.
5. **No login rate limiting / no failed-login logging**: credential-stuffing risk, worse for a privileged admin path.
6. **Wildcard redirect** (`App.tsx:89-90`) instead of 404 discloses the admin landing to customers.
7. **Uploads on local disk** (`backend/uploads/`): works single-instance; multi-instance deploys need shared storage. Filename includes org_id (info leak in backups, minor).
8. **CORS** (`middleware.go:111-136`): strict allowlist, but `Access-Control-Allow-Headers/Methods` are only set when `Origin` matches — fine; cookie scope N/A (no cookies). When splitting lifetimes/cookies later, set `Path=/api/v1/admin` vs `/api/v1` + `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite` to contain scope.

## (b) Gaps versus the goal

1. **Two login paths / audiences / lifetimes**: missing entirely. One endpoint, one token, one TTL, one storage key.
2. **`cmd/seed-admin` + no-`ADMIN_EMAILS`**: **already satisfied** — nothing to do except keep it and add admin-invite later.
3. **DB-check-per-request for admin**: **already satisfied** (`IsAdmin` per request).
4. **Reg → verify → org → sandbox → KYC → approve → live**: ~80% built (register, OTP, orgs, KYC submit/queue/decide, sandbox gate, banner). Missing: email-verification **enforcement**, admin **suspend/unsuspend**, per-org **fee** override (only limits exist), **audit rows**, **customer notification** on decision, **TOTP hook**.
5. **Frontend split**: missing entirely (layouts, contexts, clients, guards, routes, 404, admin visual identity).
6. **Tests/docs for partition**: missing (no cross-audience tests possible — no audiences; README documents the old single-login world).

## (c) Implementation plan (numbered, in order)

> Recommendation: **Option B** (one `users` table + `kind admin|customer` column, separate login endpoints, `aud=admin|customer` claim, separate TTLs, DB kind+admin check per request). Reason: the tree already FKeys `otp_codes.user_id → users`, `org_members.user_id` is a bare UUID matched against `users.id` in service code, and `seed-admin` promotes in place. Option A (two tables) would force rewriting every membership/OTP/KYC-review join and the promote flow for **zero additional security** once `aud` + per-request DB checks are enforced. The security boundary comes from audience validation + DB kind check, not table count.

0. **Prep (no behavior change)**: back up DB; record route inventory (§2) as the test matrix; decide open questions (d) below.
1. **Migration `000044_identity_partition`**: `ALTER users ADD kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'customer' CHECK (kind IN ('admin','customer'))`; backfill `kind='admin'` where `is_admin`; add `email_verified_at` NOT NULL-soft gate column already exists — no change; create `app.audit_log(actor_id, actor_email, action, target_type, target_id, before, after, ip, created_at)` + `app.login_attempts` (optional, for rate-limit/audit); down migration reverses. Never edit past migrations.
2. **Backend auth**: `Claims` += `aud`; `Verifier` += `expectedAud` + per-audience TTL (`AUTH_CUSTOMER_TOKEN_TTL`, `AUTH_ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL`); `IssueCustomerToken` / `IssueAdminToken`; `RequireCustomerAuth` (aud=customer + kind=customer DB check) and `RequireAdminAuth` (aud=admin + kind=admin + is_admin DB check); wrong-audience → `401 invalid_audience` / `403 wrong_space` JSON. New handlers `POST /api/v1/auth/register|login` (customer-only; register forces `kind=customer`, requires email verify before full access) and `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login` (+ optional invite-accept `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/invite`); stricter admin rate limit + failed-login audit rows + TOTP hook point. Keep `seed-admin` as the only admin mint (plus admin-invite).
3. **Routes**: rewire `app.go` into three groups — `/api/v1/admin/...` → `RequireAdminAuth`, `/api/v1/...` (orgs/merchant/auth) → `RequireCustomerAuth`, `/api/v1/payments/...` → API-key only. Relocate identity to `GET /api/v1/auth/me` (customer) and `GET /api/v1/admin/auth/me` (admin); keep `/api/v1/admin/me` as deprecated alias for one release if needed.
4. **Customer hardening**: enforce `email_verified_at` before org/dashboard access (allow OTP + KYC-status reads); keep sandbox/live gates as-is (already service-layer).
5. **Admin controls**: `suspended` columns (orgs/apps), suspend/unsuspend endpoints, per-org fee override endpoints, every admin mutation → `audit_log` row, approve/reject → mailer-interface email (log stub until provider wired).
6. **Frontend split**: `AdminAuthContext` (`lipago_admin_token`) + `CustomerAuthContext` (`lipago_customer_token`) + two API clients; `AdminLayout` (ADMIN bar, admin nav only) vs `CustomerLayout` (org switcher, sandbox/live badge, KYC banner); move pages (`Admin*` → `/admin/...`, merchant/org/onboarding → customer space); new `/login /register /verify-email /onboarding/... /dashboard`, `/admin/login /admin ...`; 404 for guessed `/admin` URLs as customer.
7. **Tests + docs**: table-driven cross-audience rejection over the §2 inventory; registration-never-admin; unverified-live-block; KYC transitions; revocation-immediacy; cross-org denial; frontend guard tests; README/API-docs update (two logins, audiences, groups, KYC diagram, seed-first-admin).

2. **Existing sessions**: revoke-all on deploy (simplest, given no `aud` in old tokens) vs. grace period accepting legacy tokens? I recommend revoke-all + re-login.
3. **Email-verification enforcement**: block dashboard/org access until verified (strict, per brief) vs. allow sandbox immediately and gate only live actions? Brief says "required before dashboard access" — confirm strict.

## Option A vs Option B — Identity Separation

### Option A: Separate tables (`admin_users` + `users`)

- Two physical tables. Two password hashes. Two login handlers. Two token audiences (`aud=admin` vs `aud=customer`), optionally two signing keys.
- Admin auth checks `admin_users`. Customer auth checks `users`. A token from one table is structurally meaningless in the other space.

**Pros:**
- Strongest physical isolation. A SQL mix-up (`WHERE id = ...` on the wrong table) fails closed instead of leaking.
- Admin and customer schemas can evolve independently (e.g. TOTP secret, failed-login counters only on `admin_users`).
- Easy to reason about in audits: "admins live here, customers live there."

**Cons (specific to this repo):**
- Everything that references "a user" must be rewired or duplicated: `app.otp_codes.user_id → users`, `app.org_members.user_id` (bare UUID matched against `users.id` in service code), KYC `reviewed_by`, withdrawal `requested_by/approved_by`, invites by email.
- `cmd/seed-admin` promote-in-place becomes migrate-row-instead-of-promote. Every join becomes a UNION or a second query.
- Higher migration risk: moving existing `is_admin=true` rows to a new table, backfilling FKs, keeping down-migration safe.

### Option B: One `users` table + `kind` column

- One table: `users(id, email, password_hash, kind admin|customer, is_admin, ...)`.
- Still **two separate login endpoints**, **two token audiences**, **two lifetimes**:
  - `POST /api/v1/auth/login` → `aud=customer`, long TTL
  - `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login` → `aud=admin`, short TTL
- Every request enforces **audience + DB kind check**: customer middleware accepts only (`aud=customer` AND `kind=customer`); admin middleware accepts only (`aud=admin` AND `kind=admin` AND `is_admin`).
- Public registration hard-forces `kind=customer`. Admins only via `seed-admin` or admin-invite.

**Pros:**
- Fits this codebase: OTP, org membership, KYC review, withdrawals all keep working with zero FK rewrites — one `ALTER TABLE ... ADD kind` + backfill (`kind='admin'` where `is_admin`).
- Security boundary is identical in practice once `aud` + per-request DB check is enforced: a stolen customer token is rejected on admin routes with 401/403 even if `user_id` matches, and vice versa.
- Smaller, safer migration. Easier down-migration.

**Cons:**
- Logical separation, not physical. A future code bug that forgets the `aud`/`kind` check could cross spaces — mitigated by centralizing the check in the two middleware chains (only place that validates identity) plus table-driven cross-audience tests over the full route inventory.
- Admin-only columns (TOTP secret, lockout counters) sit nullable on the shared table.

### My recommendation for your repo: **B**

Your tree already has `IsAdmin()` re-read from the DB per request, `seed-admin` promote-in-place, and a half-dozen features keyed off `users.id`. The real partition defect is **no audience + shared token**, not shared storage. B fixes the actual hole with one migration; A rewrites identity plumbing for no additional runtime security.

Pick A only if you need compliance-grade physical separation of admin credentials (separate table, separate keys, separate rotation policy) and accept the larger migration + dual-query cost everywhere.

101: // SlugFor generates a URL-safe unique slug for a new org.
102: func SlugFor(name string) string {
103: 	base := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
104: 	var cleaned strings.Builder
105: 	for _, r := range base {
106: 		switch {
107: 		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
108: 			cleaned.WriteRune(r)
109: 		case r == ' ' || r == '-' || r == '_':
110: 			cleaned.WriteRune('-')
111: 		}
112: 	}
113: 	slug := strings.Trim(cleaned.String(), "-")
114: 	if len(slug) > 40 {
115: 		slug = slug[:40]
116: 	}
117: 	if slug == "" {
118: 		slug = "org"
119: 	}
120: 	suffix := make([]byte, 3)
121: 	if _, err := rand.Read(suffix); err != nil {
122: 		return slug + "-000000"
123: 	}
124: 	return slug + "-" + hex.EncodeToString(suffix)
125: }

439: func scanKYCSubmission(row interface{ Scan(dest ...interface{}) error }) (KYCSubmission, error) {
440: 	var sub KYCSubmission
441: 	var reviewedBy, rejectionReason sql.NullString
442: 	var reviewedAt sql.NullTime
443: 	if err := row.Scan(
444: 		&sub.OrgID, &sub.BusinessName, &sub.TIN, &sub.IDDocumentURL,
445: 		&sub.SubmittedAt, &reviewedBy, &reviewedAt, &rejectionReason,
446: 	); err != nil {
447: 		return KYCSubmission{}, err
448: 	}
449: 	sub.ReviewedBy = reviewedBy.String
450: 	if reviewedAt.Valid {
451: 		sub.ReviewedAt = &reviewedAt.Time
452: 	}
453: 	sub.RejectionReason = rejectionReason.String
454: 	return sub, nil
455: }

457: const kycSubmissionSelect = `
458: 	SELECT org_id::text, business_name, tin, id_document_url, submitted_at,
459: 	       reviewed_by, reviewed_at, COALESCE(rejection_reason, '')
460: 	FROM app.kyc_submissions
461: `
462:
463: // SubmitKYC records (or resubmits) verification evidence and flips the org
464: // to submitted. Resubmission clears any prior review outcome.
465: func (r *PostgresRepository) SubmitKYC(ctx context.Context, orgID, businessName, tin, docURL string) (KYCSubmission, error) {
466: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginEx(ctx, nil)
467: 	if err != nil {
468: 		return KYCSubmission{}, fmt.Errorf("begin submit kyc transaction: %w", err)
469: 	}
470: 	defer func() {
471: 		if err != nil {
472: 			_ = tx.RollbackEx(ctx)
473: 		}
474: 	}()
475:
476: 	if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `
477: 		INSERT INTO app.kyc_submissions (org_id, business_name, tin, id_document_url)
478: 		VALUES ($1::uuid, $2, $3, $4)
479: 		ON CONFLICT (org_id) DO UPDATE SET
480: 			business_name = EXCLUDED.business_name,
481: 			tin = EXCLUDED.tin,
482: 			id_document_url = EXCLUDED.id_document_url,
483: 			submitted_at = NOW(),
484: 			reviewed_by = NULL,
485: 			reviewed_at = NULL,
486: 			rejection_reason = ''
487: 	`, nil, orgID, businessName, tin, docURL); err != nil {
488: 		return KYCSubmission{}, fmt.Errorf("upsert kyc submission: %w", err)
489: 	}
490: 	if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `
491: 		UPDATE app.organizations SET business_name = $2, tin = $3, kyc_status = 'submitted', updated_at = NOW()
492: 		WHERE id = $1::uuid
493: 	`, nil, orgID, valueOrNil(businessName), valueOrNil(tin)); err != nil {
494: 		return KYCSubmission{}, fmt.Errorf("mark org kyc submitted: %w", err)
495: 	}
496: 	var sub KYCSubmission
497: 	sub, err = scanKYCSubmission(tx.QueryRowEx(ctx, kycSubmissionSelect+` WHERE org_id = $1::uuid`, nil, orgID))
498: 	if err != nil {
499: 		return KYCSubmission{}, fmt.Errorf("load kyc submission: %w", err)
500: 	}
501: 	if err = tx.CommitEx(ctx); err != nil {
502: 		return KYCSubmission{}, fmt.Errorf("commit submit kyc transaction: %w", err)
503: 	}
504: 	return sub, nil
505: }
506:
507: // GetKYCSubmission loads the evidence row; found=false when never submitted.
508: func (r *PostgresRepository) GetKYCSubmission(ctx context.Context, orgID string) (KYCSubmission, bool, error) {
509: 	sub, err := scanKYCSubmission(r.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, kycSubmissionSelect+` WHERE org_id = $1::uuid`, nil, orgID))
510: 	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
511: 		return KYCSubmission{}, false, nil
512: 	}
513: 	if err != nil {
514: 		return KYCSubmission{}, false, fmt.Errorf("get kyc submission: %w", err)
515: 	}
516: 	return sub, true, nil
517: }

519: // ReviewKYC records an admin decision. Only orgs sitting in submitted
520: // with a live submission row are reviewable — approving thin air (or
521: // re-deciding a closed file) is refused so the queue can't be bypassed.
522: func (r *PostgresRepository) ReviewKYC(ctx context.Context, orgID, status, reviewedBy, reason string) (Organization, error) {
523: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginEx(ctx, nil)
524: 	if err != nil {
525: 		return Organization{}, fmt.Errorf("begin review kyc transaction: %w", err)
526: 	}
527: 	defer func() {
528: 		if err != nil {
529: 			_ = tx.RollbackEx(ctx)
530: 		}
531: 	}()
532:
533: 	var current string
534: 	err = tx.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT kyc_status FROM app.organizations WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, orgID).Scan(&current)
535: 	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
536: 		return Organization{}, ErrOrgNotFound
537: 	}
538: 	if err != nil {
539: 		return Organization{}, fmt.Errorf("load org kyc status: %w", err)
540: 	}
541: 	if current != "submitted" {
542: 		return Organization{}, ErrKYCNotInReview
543: 	}
544: 	var hasSubmission bool
545: 	err = tx.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM app.kyc_submissions WHERE org_id = $1::uuid)`, nil, orgID).Scan(&hasSubmission)
546: 	if err != nil {
547: 		return Organization{}, fmt.Errorf("check kyc submission: %w", err)
548: 	}
549: 	if !hasSubmission {
550: 		return Organization{}, ErrKYCNotInReview
551: 	}
552:
553: 	if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `
554: 		UPDATE app.kyc_submissions
555: 		SET reviewed_by = $2, reviewed_at = NOW(), rejection_reason = $3
556: 		WHERE org_id = $1::uuid
557: 	`, nil, orgID, valueOrNil(reviewedBy), reason); err != nil {
558: 		return Organization{}, fmt.Errorf("record kyc review: %w", err)
559: 	}
560: 	var org Organization
561: 	org, err = scanOrganization(tx.QueryRowEx(ctx, `
562: 		UPDATE app.organizations SET kyc_status = $2, updated_at = NOW()
563: 		WHERE id = $1::uuid
564: 		RETURNING id::text, name, slug, kyc_status, business_name, tin,
565: 		          live_max_txn_amount, live_daily_volume_cap, created_at, updated_at
566: 	`, nil, orgID, status))
567: 	if err != nil {
568: 		return Organization{}, fmt.Errorf("mark org kyc reviewed: %w", err)
569: 	}
570: 	if err = tx.CommitEx(ctx); err != nil {
571: 		return Organization{}, fmt.Errorf("commit review kyc transaction: %w", err)
572: 	}
573: 	return org, nil
574: }
575:
576: // ListKYCQueue returns orgs holding submissions, newest first. Empty
577: // status selects submitted (the actionable queue).
578: func (r *PostgresRepository) ListKYCQueue(ctx context.Context, status string) ([]KYCQueueItem, error) {
579: 	status = strings.TrimSpace(status)
580: 	args := []any{}
581: 	condition := ""
582: 	if status == "" {
583: 		status = "submitted"
584: 	}
585: 	if status != "all" {
586: 		condition = "WHERE o.kyc_status = $1"
587: 		args = append(args, status)
588: 	}
589: 	rows, err := r.db.QueryEx(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(`
590: 		SELECT o.id::text, o.name, o.slug, o.kyc_status,
591: 		       COALESCE(s.business_name, ''), COALESCE(s.tin, ''),
592: 		       COALESCE(s.id_document_url, '') <> '',
593: 		       s.submitted_at, COALESCE(s.rejection_reason, '')
594: 		FROM app.organizations o
595: 		JOIN app.kyc_submissions s ON s.org_id = o.id
596: 		%s
597: 		ORDER BY s.submitted_at DESC
598: 	`, condition), nil, args...)
599: 	if err != nil {
600: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("list kyc queue: %w", err)
601: 	}
602: 	defer rows.Close()
603:
604: 	items := []KYCQueueItem{}
605: 	for rows.Next() {
606: 		var item KYCQueueItem
607: 		if err := rows.Scan(
608: 			&item.OrgID, &item.OrgName, &item.Slug, &item.KYCStatus,
609: 			&item.BusinessName, &item.TIN, &item.HasDocument,
610: 			&item.SubmittedAt, &item.RejectionReason,
611: 		); err != nil {
612: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan kyc queue item: %w", err)
613: 		}
614: 		items = append(items, item)
615: 	}
616: 	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
617: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("iterate kyc queue: %w", err)
618: 	}
619: 	return items, nil
620: }

624: func (r *PostgresRepository) UpdateOrgLiveLimits(ctx context.Context, orgID, maxTxn, dailyCap string) (Organization, error) {

631: 		RETURNING id::text, name, slug, kyc_status, business_name, tin,

43: // checks against the matching table.
44: const (
45: 	AudienceCustomer = "customer"
46: 	AudienceAdmin    = "admin"
47: )
48:
49: // claimsKey stores verified Claims on the request context. Defined here
50: // (not in middleware) so auth handlers can read claims without importing
51: // middleware — middleware imports auth, so the reverse would cycle.
52: type claimsKey struct{}
53:
54: // WithClaims returns a context carrying verified Claims.
55: func WithClaims(ctx context.Context, claims Claims) context.Context {
56: 	return context.WithValue(ctx, claimsKey{}, claims)
57: }
58:
59: // ClaimsFromContext returns verified Claims from the request context.
60: func ClaimsFromContext(ctx context.Context) (Claims, bool) {
61: 	claims, ok := ctx.Value(claimsKey{}).(Claims)
62: 	return claims, ok
63: }
64:
65: type User struct {
66: 	ID, Email, PasswordHash string
67: 	IsAdmin                 bool
68: }
69:
70: type Verifier struct {
71: 	secret   []byte
72: 	tokenTTL time.Duration
73: 	audience string
74: }
75:
76: // NewVerifier keeps its original signature for compatibility and returns
77: // the CUSTOMER verifier (aud=customer).
78: func NewVerifier(cfg config.AuthConfig, _ any) *Verifier {
79: 	return NewCustomerVerifier(cfg, nil)
80: }
81:
82: // NewCustomerVerifier validates customer-space tokens (aud=customer).
83: func NewCustomerVerifier(cfg config.AuthConfig, _ any) *Verifier {
84: 	return &Verifier{secret: []byte(cfg.JWTSecret), tokenTTL: cfg.TokenTTL, audience: AudienceCustomer}
85: }
86:
87: // NewAdminVerifier validates admin-space tokens (aud=admin). It uses
88: // AUTH_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET when set, otherwise falls back to the customer
89: // secret — audience separation still rejects cross-use either way.
90: func NewAdminVerifier(cfg config.AuthConfig, _ any) *Verifier {
91: 	secret := strings.TrimSpace(cfg.AdminJWTSecret)
92: 	if secret == "" {
93: 		secret = cfg.JWTSecret
94: 	}
95: 	ttl := cfg.AdminTokenTTL
96: 	if ttl <= 0 {
97: 		ttl = cfg.TokenTTL
98: 	}
99: 	return &Verifier{secret: []byte(secret), tokenTTL: ttl, audience: AudienceAdmin}
100: }
101:
102: func (v *Verifier) Audience() string { return v.audience }
103:
104: func (v *Verifier) IssueToken(user User) (string, error) {
105: 	now := time.Now().Unix()
106: 	claims := Claims{Subject: user.ID, Email: user.Email, IsAdmin: user.IsAdmin, Audience: v.audience, IssuedAt: now, Expiry: now + int64(v.tokenTTL.Seconds())}
107: 	header, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"})
108: 	payload, err := json.Marshal(claims)
109: 	if err != nil {
110: 		return "", err
111: 	}
112: 	encodedHeader := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(header)
113: 	encodedPayload := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(payload)
114: 	input := encodedHeader + "." + encodedPayload
115: 	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, v.secret)
116: 	_, _ = mac.Write([]byte(input))
117: 	return input + "." + base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil)), nil
118: }
119:
120: func (v *Verifier) VerifyBearerToken(_ context.Context, token string) (Claims, error) {
121: 	parts := strings.Split(token, ".")
122: 	if len(parts) != 3 {
123: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("invalid token format")
124: 	}
125: 	headerBytes, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[0])
126: 	if err != nil {
127: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("invalid token header")
128: 	}
129: 	var header struct {
130: 		Algorithm string `json:"alg"`
131: 	}
132: 	if json.Unmarshal(headerBytes, &header) != nil || header.Algorithm != "HS256" {
133: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("unsupported token algorithm")
134: 	}
135: 	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, v.secret)
136: 	_, _ = mac.Write([]byte(parts[0] + "." + parts[1]))
137: 	signature, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[2])
138: 	if err != nil || !hmac.Equal(mac.Sum(nil), signature) {
139: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("invalid token signature")
140: 	}
141: 	payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[1])
142: 	if err != nil {
143: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("invalid token payload")
144: 	}
145: 	var claims Claims
146: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &claims); err != nil {
147: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("invalid token claims")
148: 	}
149: 	if claims.Subject == "" || claims.Email == "" || time.Now().Unix() >= claims.Expiry {
150: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("token expired or invalid")
151: 	}
152: 	// Audience partition: a token minted for one space is unusable in the
153: 	// other even if the user_id somehow matches a row there.
154: 	if v.audience != "" && claims.Audience != "" && claims.Audience != v.audience {
155: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("invalid token audience")
156: 	}
157: 	if v.audience != "" && claims.Audience == "" {
158: 		return Claims{}, errors.New("invalid token audience")
159: 	}
160: 	return claims, nil
161: }

163: type Service struct {
164: 	db                  *pgx.ConnPool
165: 	verifier            *Verifier // customer verifier (back-compat)
166: 	customerVerifier    *Verifier

170: 	sms                 SMSSender

174: 	// func(secret, code string) bool. Nil means "no TOTP provider wired".
175: 	TOTPVerify func(secret, code string) bool
176: }

179: 	return &Service{

181: 		customerVerifier: verifier,

183: 		adminLoginLimiter: newRateLimiter(5, time.Minute),

199: // SetLoginRateLimits overrides the default 20/min customer and 5/min
200: // admin login caps (from AUTH_LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN and
201: // AUTH_ADMIN_LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN).
202: func (s *Service) SetLoginRateLimits(customerPerMin, adminPerMin int) {
203: 	if customerPerMin > 0 {
204: 		s.loginLimiter = newRateLimiter(customerPerMin, time.Minute)
205: 	}

207: 		s.adminLoginLimiter = newRateLimiter(adminPerMin, time.Minute)

210:
211: // rateLimiter is a minimal in-memory sliding-window limiter (per key).
212: type rateLimiter struct {
213: 	max    int
214: 	window time.Duration
215: 	mu     sync.Mutex
216: 	hits   map[string][]time.Time
217: }
218:
219: func newRateLimiter(max int, window time.Duration) *rateLimiter {
220: 	return &rateLimiter{max: max, window: window, hits: map[string][]time.Time{}}
221: }
222:
223: // Allow reports whether key may proceed (recording the hit).
224: func (l *rateLimiter) Allow(key string) bool {
225: 	if l == nil || l.max <= 0 {
226: 		return true
227: 	}
228: 	now := time.Now()
229: 	cutoff := now.Add(-l.window)
230: 	l.mu.Lock()
231: 	defer l.mu.Unlock()
232: 	kept := l.hits[key][:0]
233: 	for _, t := range l.hits[key] {
234: 		if t.After(cutoff) {
235: 			kept = append(kept, t)
236: 		}
237: 	}
238: 	if len(kept) >= l.max {
239: 		l.hits[key] = kept
240: 		return false
241: 	}
242: 	l.hits[key] = append(kept, now)
243: 	return true
244: }
245:
246: // clientIP extracts the request IP for rate limiting / audit.
247: func clientIP(r *http.Request) string {
248: 	if r == nil {
249: 		return ""
250: 	}
251: 	if forwarded := strings.TrimSpace(r.Header.Get("X-Forwarded-For")); forwarded != "" {
252: 		if idx := strings.Index(forwarded, ","); idx >= 0 {
253: 			return strings.TrimSpace(forwarded[:idx])
254: 		}
255: 		return forwarded
256: 	}
257: 	host, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(strings.TrimSpace(r.RemoteAddr))
258: 	if err != nil {
259: 		return strings.TrimSpace(r.RemoteAddr)
260: 	}
261: 	return host
262: }

283: // SetAllowPublicRegister opens POST /api/v1/auth/register to anyone.
284: // Default closed: registration is allowed only for the very first account
285: // (empty users table) so a fresh deployment can bootstrap its admin, then
286: // closed. Additional accounts must be created by an operator while closed.

288: 	s.allowPublicRegister = allow
289: }

291: // ErrPublicRegistrationDisabled is returned when self-registration is
292: // attempted after the bootstrap account already exists.
293: var ErrPublicRegistrationDisabled = errors.New("public registration is disabled")
294:
295: func (s *Service) customerTokens() *Verifier {
296: 	if s.customerVerifier != nil {
297: 		return s.customerVerifier
298: 	}
299: 	return s.verifier
300: }

302: func (s *Service) adminTokens() *Verifier {
303: 	if s.adminVerifier != nil {
304: 		return s.adminVerifier

308:
309: func (s *Service) Register(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (User, string, error) {
310: 	email = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(email))
311: 	if !strings.Contains(email, "@") || len(password) < 12 {
312: 		return User{}, "", errors.New("use a valid email and a password with at least 12 characters")
313: 	}
314: 	if !s.allowPublicRegister && !s.isFirstUser(ctx) {
315: 		return User{}, "", ErrPublicRegistrationDisabled
316: 	}
317: 	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
318: 	if err != nil {
319: 		return User{}, "", fmt.Errorf("hash password: %w", err)
320: 	}
321: 	// Self-registration creates CUSTOMER accounts only (app.users, never
322: 	// admin). There is no allowlist, no flag, no email that can mint an
323: 	// operator — admins exist solely in app.admin_users via seed/invite.
324: 	u := User{ID: uuid.NewString(), Email: email, PasswordHash: string(hash), IsAdmin: false}
325: 	err = s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `INSERT INTO app.users (id, email, password_hash, is_admin) VALUES ($1::uuid, $2, $3, $4) RETURNING id::text, email, password_hash, is_admin`, nil, u.ID, u.Email, u.PasswordHash, u.IsAdmin).Scan(&u.ID, &u.Email, &u.PasswordHash, &u.IsAdmin)
326: 	if err != nil {
327: 		if pgErr, ok := err.(pgx.PgError); ok && pgErr.Code == "23505" {
328: 			return User{}, "", errors.New("an account already exists for this email")
329: 		}
330: 		return User{}, "", fmt.Errorf("create user: %w", err)
331: 	}
332: 	u.IsAdmin = false
333: 	token, err := s.customerTokens().IssueToken(u)
334: 	return u, token, err
335: }
336:
337: func (s *Service) Login(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (User, string, error) {
338: 	email = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(email))
339: 	var u User
340: 	err := s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT id::text, email, password_hash, is_admin FROM app.users WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)`, nil, email).Scan(&u.ID, &u.Email, &u.PasswordHash, &u.IsAdmin)
341: 	if err != nil || bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(password)) != nil {
342: 		return User{}, "", errors.New("invalid email or password")
343: 	}
344: 	u.IsAdmin = false
345: 	token, err := s.customerTokens().IssueToken(u)
346: 	return u, token, err
347: }
348:
349: // isFirstUser reports whether no accounts exist yet (fresh deployment).
350: // Registration failures here fail closed (treated as "not first").
351: func (s *Service) isFirstUser(ctx context.Context) bool {
352: 	var count int64
353: 	if err := s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM app.users`, nil).Scan(&count); err != nil {
354: 		return false
355: 	}
356: 	return count == 0
357: }

387: // CustomerEmailVerified reports whether the customer completed email
388: // verification. Dashboard/org access requires this (OTP + status reads
389: // stay open so users can finish verifying).
390: func (s *Service) CustomerEmailVerified(ctx context.Context, userID string) (bool, error) {
391: 	var verifiedAt sql.NullTime
392: 	err := s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT email_verified_at FROM app.users WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, userID).Scan(&verifiedAt)
393: 	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
394: 		return false, nil
395: 	}
396: 	if err != nil {
397: 		return false, err
398: 	}
399: 	return verifiedAt.Valid, nil
400: }

402: // WriteAudit records an admin-space action. Best-effort: audit failures
403: // are returned so callers can log them, but must never grant access.
404: func (s *Service) WriteAudit(ctx context.Context, actorID, actorEmail, action, targetType, targetID, ip string, before, after map[string]any) error {
405: 	var beforeJSON, afterJSON *string
406: 	if before != nil {
407: 		if raw, err := json.Marshal(before); err == nil {
408: 			str := string(raw)
409: 			beforeJSON = &str
410: 		}
411: 	}
412: 	if after != nil {
413: 		if raw, err := json.Marshal(after); err == nil {
414: 			str := string(raw)
415: 			afterJSON = &str
416: 		}
417: 	}
418: 	_, err := s.db.ExecEx(ctx, `INSERT INTO app.audit_log (actor_id, actor_email, action, target_type, target_id, before_data, after_data, ip) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6::jsonb, $7::jsonb, $8)`,
419: 		nil, actorID, actorEmail, action, targetType, targetID, beforeJSON, afterJSON, ip)
420: 	return err
421: }
422:
423: // ---------- Admin identity (Option A: app.admin_users) ----------
424:
425: // AdminUser is a platform operator (separate table, separate hashes,
426: // separate tokens from customers).
427: type AdminUser struct {
428: 	ID, Email, PasswordHash string
429: }
430:
431: var (
432: 	ErrAdminInvalidCredentials = errors.New("invalid email or password")
433: 	ErrAdminLocked             = errors.New("account temporarily locked after too many failed attempts")
434: 	ErrTOTPRequired            = errors.New("two-factor code required")
435: 	ErrTOTPInvalid             = errors.New("invalid two-factor code")
436: )
437:
438: // AdminLogin authenticates an operator against app.admin_users and issues
439: // an admin-audience token (short TTL). Failures are audit-logged; repeated
440: // failures lock the account briefly. TOTP: when the row carries a
441: // totp_secret and a TOTPVerify hook is wired, the code must verify;
442: // when a secret exists but no hook is wired, login stops with
443: // ErrTOTPRequired so 2FA cannot be silently skipped later.
444: func (s *Service) AdminLogin(ctx context.Context, email, password, totpCode, ip string) (AdminUser, string, error) {
445: 	email = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(email))
446: 	var u AdminUser
447: 	var totpSecret string
448: 	var failedAttempts int
449: 	var lockedUntil sql.NullTime
450: 	err := s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT id::text, email, password_hash, COALESCE(totp_secret, ''), COALESCE(failed_attempts, 0), locked_until FROM app.admin_users WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)`, nil, email).Scan(
451: 		&u.ID, &u.Email, &u.PasswordHash, &totpSecret, &failedAttempts, &lockedUntil)
452: 	if err != nil {
453: 		_ = s.WriteAudit(ctx, "", email, "admin.login_failed", "admin_user", "", ip, nil, map[string]any{"reason": "unknown_email"})
454: 		return AdminUser{}, "", ErrAdminInvalidCredentials
455: 	}
456: 	if lockedUntil.Valid && time.Now().Before(lockedUntil.Time) {
457: 		_ = s.WriteAudit(ctx, u.ID, u.Email, "admin.login_blocked_locked", "admin_user", u.ID, ip, nil, nil)
458: 		return AdminUser{}, "", ErrAdminLocked
459: 	}
460: 	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(password)) != nil {
461: 		failedAttempts++
462: 		lockClause := ""
463: 		if failedAttempts >= 5 {
464: 			lockClause = ", locked_until = NOW() + INTERVAL '15 minutes', failed_attempts = 0"
465: 		} else {
466: 			lockClause = fmt.Sprintf(", failed_attempts = %d", failedAttempts)
467: 		}
468: 		_, _ = s.db.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.admin_users SET updated_at = NOW()`+lockClause+` WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, u.ID)
469: 		_ = s.WriteAudit(ctx, u.ID, u.Email, "admin.login_failed", "admin_user", u.ID, ip, nil, map[string]any{"reason": "bad_password"})
470: 		if failedAttempts >= 5 {
471: 			return AdminUser{}, "", ErrAdminLocked
472: 		}
473: 		return AdminUser{}, "", ErrAdminInvalidCredentials
474: 	}
475: 	if strings.TrimSpace(totpSecret) != "" {
476: 		if s.TOTPVerify == nil {
477: 			return AdminUser{}, "", ErrTOTPRequired
478: 		}
479: 		if !s.TOTPVerify(totpSecret, strings.TrimSpace(totpCode)) {
480: 			_ = s.WriteAudit(ctx, u.ID, u.Email, "admin.login_failed", "admin_user", u.ID, ip, nil, map[string]any{"reason": "bad_totp"})
481: 			return AdminUser{}, "", ErrTOTPInvalid
482: 		}
483: 	}
484: 	_, _ = s.db.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.admin_users SET failed_attempts = 0, locked_until = NULL, last_login_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, u.ID)
485: 	_ = s.WriteAudit(ctx, u.ID, u.Email, "admin.login", "admin_user", u.ID, ip, nil, nil)
486: 	token, err := s.adminTokens().IssueToken(User{ID: u.ID, Email: u.Email, IsAdmin: true})
487: 	return u, token, err
488: }
489:
490: // AdminInviteUser creates another operator. Callable only by an existing
491: // admin (route-gated AND re-checked here from the DB). ctx must carry
492: // admin claims (set by RequireAdminAuth).
493: func (s *Service) AdminInviteUser(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (AdminUser, error) {
494: 	claims, ok := ClaimsFromContext(ctx)
495: 	if !ok {
496: 		return AdminUser{}, errors.New("missing authenticated admin")
497: 	}
498: 	if claims.Audience != "" && claims.Audience != AudienceAdmin {
499: 		return AdminUser{}, errors.New("wrong token audience")
500: 	}
501: 	isAdmin, err := s.IsAdminUser(ctx, claims.Subject)
502: 	if err != nil || !isAdmin {
503: 		return AdminUser{}, errors.New("insufficient privileges")
504: 	}
505: 	email = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(email))
506: 	if !strings.Contains(email, "@") || len(password) < 12 {
507: 		return AdminUser{}, errors.New("use a valid email and a password with at least 12 characters")
508: 	}
509: 	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
510: 	if err != nil {
511: 		return AdminUser{}, fmt.Errorf("hash password: %w", err)
512: 	}
513: 	var u AdminUser
514: 	u = AdminUser{ID: uuid.NewString(), Email: email, PasswordHash: string(hash)}
515: 	err = s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `INSERT INTO app.admin_users (id, email, password_hash) VALUES ($1::uuid, $2, $3) RETURNING id::text, email, password_hash`, nil, u.ID, u.Email, u.PasswordHash).Scan(&u.ID, &u.Email, &u.PasswordHash)
516: 	if err != nil {
517: 		if pgErr, ok := err.(pgx.PgError); ok && pgErr.Code == "23505" {
518: 			return AdminUser{}, errors.New("an admin already exists for this email")
519: 		}
520: 		return AdminUser{}, fmt.Errorf("create admin user: %w", err)
521: 	}
522: 	_ = s.WriteAudit(ctx, claims.Subject, claims.Email, "admin.invite", "admin_user", u.ID, "", nil, map[string]any{"email": u.Email})
523: 	return u, nil
524: }
525:
526: // CreateAdminUser creates an operator directly in app.admin_users (seed
527: // script / admin invite tooling). It is the only way admin accounts come
528: // into existence — public registration writes app.users and can never
529: // grant admin.
530: func (s *Service) CreateAdminUser(ctx context.Context, email, password string) (User, error) {
531: 	email = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(email))
532: 	if !strings.Contains(email, "@") || len(password) < 12 {
533: 		return User{}, errors.New("use a valid email and a password with at least 12 characters")
534: 	}
535: 	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
536: 	if err != nil {
537: 		return User{}, fmt.Errorf("hash password: %w", err)
538: 	}
539: 	var u User
540: 	u = User{ID: uuid.NewString(), Email: email, PasswordHash: string(hash), IsAdmin: true}
541: 	err = s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `INSERT INTO app.admin_users (id, email, password_hash) VALUES ($1::uuid, $2, $3) RETURNING id::text, email, password_hash`, nil, u.ID, u.Email, u.PasswordHash).Scan(&u.ID, &u.Email, &u.PasswordHash)
542: 	if err != nil {
543: 		if pgErr, ok := err.(pgx.PgError); ok && pgErr.Code == "23505" {
544: 			return User{}, errors.New("an account already exists for this email")
545: 		}
546: 		return User{}, fmt.Errorf("create admin user: %w", err)
547: 	}
548: 	return u, nil
549: }

606:
607: // ---------- One-time passcodes ----------
608:
609: const (
610: 	// OTPChannels.
611: 	OTPChannelEmail = "email"
612: 	OTPChannelSMS   = "sms"
613: 	// OTPPurposes.
614: 	OTPPurposeEmailVerify = "email_verify"
615: 	OTPPurposePhoneVerify = "phone_verify"
616: 	OTPPurposeLogin2FA    = "login_2fa"
617:
618: 	otpCodeLength  = 6
619: 	otpTTL         = 10 * time.Minute
620: 	otpMaxPerHour  = 5
621: 	otpMaxAttempts = 5
622: )
623:
624: var (
625: 	ErrOTPNotConfigured   = errors.New("verification sending is not configured")
626: 	ErrOTPRateLimited     = errors.New("too many codes requested — try again later")
627: 	ErrOTPNoActiveCode    = errors.New("no active code — request a fresh one")
628: 	ErrOTPExpired         = errors.New("code expired — request a fresh one")
629: 	ErrOTPLocked          = errors.New("too many wrong attempts — request a fresh code")
630: 	ErrOTPInvalid         = errors.New("invalid code")
631: 	ErrPhoneInvalid       = errors.New("phone must be a Tanzanian mobile number like +255712345678")
632: 	ErrOTPSendFailed      = errors.New("failed to send verification code")
633: )
634:
635: // GenerateOTPCode returns a zero-padded 6-digit code from crypto/rand.
636: func GenerateOTPCode() (string, error) {
637: 	max := big.NewInt(1000000)
638: 	n, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, max)
639: 	if err != nil {
640: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("generate otp code: %w", err)
641: 	}
642: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%06d", n.Int64()), nil
643: }
644:
645: // ValidTanzanianPhone accepts +255 followed by 9 digits starting with 6
646: // or 7 (all TZ mobile allocations live in 2556x/2557x ranges).
647: func ValidTanzanianPhone(phone string) bool {
648: 	phone = strings.TrimSpace(phone)
649: 	if len(phone) != 13 || !strings.HasPrefix(phone, "+255") {
650: 		return false
651: 	}
652: 	if phone[4] != '6' && phone[4] != '7' {
653: 		return false
654: 	}
655: 	for _, r := range phone[5:] {
656: 		if r < '0' || r > '9' {
657: 			return false
658: 		}
659: 	}
660: 	return true
661: }
662:
663: // OTPRequest is the outcome of RequestOTP — never contains the code.
664: type OTPRequest struct {
665: 	Channel   string    `json:"channel"`
666: 	ExpiresAt time.Time `json:"expires_at"`
667: }
668:
669: // RequestOTP creates a fresh code (superseding older unconsumed ones),
670: // rate-limits issuance, and dispatches it. For SMS the number is
671: // validated as Tanzanian and stored on the account first.
672: func (s *Service) RequestOTP(ctx context.Context, userID, channel, purpose, phone string) (OTPRequest, error) {
673: 	channel = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(channel))
674: 	purpose = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(purpose))
675: 	if channel != OTPChannelEmail && channel != OTPChannelSMS {
676: 		return OTPRequest{}, errors.New("channel must be email or sms")
677: 	}
678: 	switch purpose {
679: 	case OTPPurposeEmailVerify, OTPPurposePhoneVerify, OTPPurposeLogin2FA:
680: 	default:
681: 		return OTPRequest{}, errors.New("unknown otp purpose")
682: 	}
683:
684: 	var email, currentPhone string
685: 	err := s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT email, COALESCE(phone, '') FROM app.users WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, userID).Scan(&email, &currentPhone)
686: 	if err != nil {
687: 		return OTPRequest{}, errors.New("account not found")
688: 	}
689:
690: 	destination := email
691: 	if channel == OTPChannelSMS {
692: 		phone = strings.TrimSpace(phone)
693: 		if phone == "" {
694: 			phone = currentPhone
695: 		}
696: 		if !ValidTanzanianPhone(phone) {
697: 			return OTPRequest{}, ErrPhoneInvalid
698: 		}
699: 		if _, err := s.db.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.users SET phone = $2 WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, userID, phone); err != nil {
700: 			return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("save phone number: %w", err)
701: 		}
702: 		destination = phone
703: 	}
704:
705: 	var recent int64
706: 	if err := s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM app.otp_codes WHERE user_id = $1::uuid AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'`, nil, userID).Scan(&recent); err != nil {
707: 		return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("check otp rate limit: %w", err)
708: 	}
709: 	if recent >= otpMaxPerHour {
710: 		return OTPRequest{}, ErrOTPRateLimited
711: 	}
712:
713: 	code, err := GenerateOTPCode()
714: 	if err != nil {
715: 		return OTPRequest{}, err
716: 	}
717: 	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(code), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
718: 	if err != nil {
719: 		return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("hash otp code: %w", err)
720: 	}
721: 	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(otpTTL)
722:
723: 	tx, err := s.db.BeginEx(ctx, nil)
724: 	if err != nil {
725: 		return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("begin otp transaction: %w", err)
726: 	}
727: 	defer func() {
728: 		if err != nil {
729: 			_ = tx.RollbackEx(ctx)
730: 		}
731: 	}()
732: 	// A fresh code supersedes older unconsumed ones for the same slot, so
733: 	// lockout always clears on re-request and only the newest code works.
734: 	if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.otp_codes SET consumed_at = NOW() WHERE user_id = $1::uuid AND channel = $2 AND purpose = $3 AND consumed_at IS NULL`, nil, userID, channel, purpose); err != nil {
735: 		return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("supersede old otp codes: %w", err)
736: 	}
737: 	if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `INSERT INTO app.otp_codes (user_id, channel, code_hash, purpose, expires_at) VALUES ($1::uuid, $2, $3, $4, $5)`, nil, userID, channel, string(hash), purpose, expiresAt); err != nil {
738: 		return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("store otp code: %w", err)
739: 	}
740: 	if err = tx.CommitEx(ctx); err != nil {
741: 		return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("commit otp transaction: %w", err)
742: 	}
743:
744: 	if channel == OTPChannelEmail {
745: 		if s.mailer == nil {
746: 			return OTPRequest{}, ErrOTPNotConfigured
747: 		}
748: 		if err := s.mailer.SendEmail(ctx, destination, "Your verification code", "Your LipaGO verification code is "+code+". It expires in 10 minutes."); err != nil {
749: 			return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrOTPSendFailed, err)
750: 		}
751: 	} else {
752: 		if s.sms == nil {
753: 			return OTPRequest{}, ErrOTPNotConfigured
754: 		}
755: 		if err := s.sms.SendSMS(ctx, destination, "Your LipaGO verification code is "+code+". It expires in 10 minutes."); err != nil {
756: 			return OTPRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrOTPSendFailed, err)
757: 		}
758: 	}
759: 	return OTPRequest{Channel: channel, ExpiresAt: expiresAt}, nil
760: }
761:
762: // VerifyOTP checks a code against the newest unconsumed one, marking it
763: // consumed and setting the verified flag on success. Wrong attempts
764: // increment until lockout, which only a fresh code clears.
765: func (s *Service) VerifyOTP(ctx context.Context, userID, channel, purpose, code string) error {
766: 	channel = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(channel))
767: 	purpose = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(purpose))
768: 	code = strings.TrimSpace(code)
769: 	if code == "" {
770: 		return ErrOTPInvalid
771: 	}
772:
773: 	var id, codeHash string
774: 	var attempts int
775: 	var expiresAt time.Time
776: 	err := s.db.QueryRowEx(ctx, `
777: 		SELECT id::text, code_hash, attempts, expires_at FROM app.otp_codes
778: 		WHERE user_id = $1::uuid AND channel = $2 AND purpose = $3 AND consumed_at IS NULL
779: 		ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
780: 	`, nil, userID, channel, purpose).Scan(&id, &codeHash, &attempts, &expiresAt)
781: 	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
782: 		return ErrOTPNoActiveCode
783: 	}
784: 	if err != nil {
785: 		return fmt.Errorf("load otp code: %w", err)
786: 	}
787: 	if time.Now().UTC().After(expiresAt) {
788: 		return ErrOTPExpired
789: 	}
790: 	if attempts >= otpMaxAttempts {
791: 		return ErrOTPLocked
792: 	}
793: 	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(codeHash), []byte(code)) != nil {
794: 		if _, err := s.db.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.otp_codes SET attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, id); err != nil {
795: 			return fmt.Errorf("record otp attempt: %w", err)
796: 		}
797: 		return ErrOTPInvalid
798: 	}
799:
800: 	tx, err := s.db.BeginEx(ctx, nil)
801: 	if err != nil {
802: 		return fmt.Errorf("begin otp verify transaction: %w", err)
803: 	}
804: 	defer func() {
805: 		if err != nil {
806: 			_ = tx.RollbackEx(ctx)
807: 		}
808: 	}()
809: 	if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.otp_codes SET consumed_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, id); err != nil {
810: 		return fmt.Errorf("consume otp code: %w", err)
811: 	}
812: 	switch purpose {
813: 	case OTPPurposeEmailVerify:
814: 		if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.users SET email_verified_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, userID); err != nil {
815: 			return fmt.Errorf("mark email verified: %w", err)
816: 		}
817: 	case OTPPurposePhoneVerify:
818: 		if _, err = tx.ExecEx(ctx, `UPDATE app.users SET phone_verified_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1::uuid`, nil, userID); err != nil {
819: 			return fmt.Errorf("mark phone verified: %w", err)
820: 		}
821: 	}
822: 	if err = tx.CommitEx(ctx); err != nil {
823: 		return fmt.Errorf("commit otp verify transaction: %w", err)
824: 	}
825: 	return nil
826: }

828: func (s *Service) HandleRegister(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
829: 	// Customer-space rate limit: per IP + per email.
830: 	ip := clientIP(r)
831: 	if !s.loginLimiter.Allow("register:ip:"+ip) {
832: 		httputil.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "rate_limited", "Too many attempts — try again later.", nil)
833: 		return
834: 	}
835: 	s.handleCredentials(w, r, s.Register)
836: }
837:
838: func (s *Service) HandleLogin(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
839: 	// Customer-space rate limit: per IP and per account.
840: 	ip := clientIP(r)
841: 	if !s.loginLimiter.Allow("login:ip:"+ip) {
842: 		httputil.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "rate_limited", "Too many attempts — try again later.", nil)
843: 		return
844: 	}
845: 	var peek struct {
846: 		Email string `json:"email"`
847: 	}
848: 	peekBody, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(r.Body, 16<<10))
849: 	_ = json.Unmarshal(peekBody, &peek)
850: 	r.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(peekBody))
851: 	if email := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(peek.Email)); email != "" {
852: 		if !s.loginLimiter.Allow("login:acct:"+email) {
853: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "rate_limited", "Too many attempts for this account — try again later.", nil)
854: 			return
855: 		}
856: 	}
857: 	s.handleCredentials(w, r, s.Login)
858: }

860: // HandleAdminLogin authenticates operators (separate path, separate
861: // audience, shorter TTL, stricter rate limit, audited). TOTP hook: when
862: // wired, pass {"totp_code"} alongside email/password.
863: func (s *Service) HandleAdminLogin(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
864: 	ip := clientIP(r)
865: 	if !s.adminLoginLimiter.Allow("admin:ip:"+ip) {
866: 		httputil.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "rate_limited", "Too many attempts — try again later.", nil)
867: 		return
868: 	}
869: 	var in struct {
870: 		Email    string `json:"email"`
871: 		Password string `json:"password"`
872: 		TOTPCode string `json:"totp_code"`
873: 	}
874: 	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 16<<10)
875: 	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&in); err != nil {
876: 		httputil.Error(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", "Email and password are required.", nil)
877: 		return
878: 	}
879: 	if email := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(in.Email)); email != "" {
880: 		if !s.adminLoginLimiter.Allow("admin:acct:"+email) {
881: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "rate_limited", "Too many attempts for this account — try again later.", nil)
882: 			return
883: 		}
884: 	}
885: 	u, token, err := s.AdminLogin(r.Context(), in.Email, in.Password, in.TOTPCode, ip)
886: 	if err != nil {
887: 		switch {
888: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrAdminLocked):
889: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "account_locked", "Account temporarily locked after too many failed attempts.", nil)
890: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrTOTPRequired):
891: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "totp_required", "A two-factor code is required.", nil)
892: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrTOTPInvalid):
893: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "invalid_credentials", "Invalid email, password, or two-factor code.", nil)
894: 		default:
895: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "invalid_credentials", "Invalid email or password.", nil)
896: 		}
897: 		return
898: 	}
899: 	httputil.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"data": map[string]any{"access_token": token, "user": map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email, "is_admin": true}}})
900: }

903: // RequireAdminAuth AND re-checked in AdminInviteUser from the DB.
904: func (s *Service) HandleAdminInvite(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
905: 	var in struct {
906: 		Email    string `json:"email"`
907: 		Password string `json:"password"`
908: 	}

912: 		return
913: 	}

919: 		case "use a valid email and a password with at least 12 characters":
920: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "validation_failed", err.Error(), nil)
921: 		default:

923: 		}
924: 		return
925: 	}
926: 	httputil.JSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"data": map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email}})
927: }

994: type otpRequestHTTPInput struct {
995: 	Channel string `json:"channel"`
996: 	Purpose string `json:"purpose"`
997: 	Phone   string `json:"phone"`
998: }
999:
1000: func (s *Service) HandleOTPRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1001: 	claims, ok := ClaimsFromContext(r.Context())
1002: 	if !ok {
1003: 		httputil.Error(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "Missing authenticated user.", nil)
1004: 		return
1005: 	}
1006: 	var in otpRequestHTTPInput
1007: 	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&in); err != nil {
1008: 		httputil.Error(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request", "Channel and purpose are required.", nil)
1009: 		return
1010: 	}
1011: 	result, err := s.RequestOTP(r.Context(), claims.Subject, in.Channel, in.Purpose, in.Phone)
1012: 	if err != nil {
1013: 		switch {
1014: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrOTPRateLimited):
1015: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "rate_limited", "Too many codes requested — try again later.", nil)
1016: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrOTPNotConfigured):
1017: 			httputil.Error(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "otp_not_configured", "Verification sending is not configured on this deployment.", nil)
1018: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrPhoneInvalid):

# Phase 1 complete (Option A, backend) — committed as `0705796`

## What changed

**Identity storage** — `backend/migrations/000044_admin_identity_split.up/.down.sql` (new):
- `app.admin_users` (own password hashes, `totp_secret` hook column, `failed_attempts`/`locked_until`, `last_login_at`). Existing `is_admin=true` rows copied over, then `app.users.is_admin` cleared so the customer table can never confer admin.
- `app.audit_log` (actor, action, target, before/after JSONB, ip, timestamp).
- Down migration restores `is_admin=true` by email and drops both tables. Back up `app.users` first (`pg_dump`). Applied to your dev DB successfully.

**Tokens** — `internal/platform/auth/auth.go`:
- `Claims` gains `aud`. `NewCustomerVerifier` (`aud=customer`, `AUTH_TOKEN_TTL` 24h) and `NewAdminVerifier` (`aud=admin`, `AUTH_ADMIN_TOKEN_TTL` 4h, `AUTH_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET` with fallback). Legacy no-`aud` tokens rejected by both spaces — all sessions re-login on deploy.
- Customer `Register`/`Login` read/write `app.users` only, always `is_admin=false`. New `AdminLogin` (lockout after 5 fails/15 min, audit-logged, TOTP hook via `TOTPVerify`), `AdminInviteUser` (DB re-check), `HandleCustomerMe` / `HandleAdminMe`, audit writer, per-IP + per-account rate limiters (20/min customer, 5/min admin, env-overridable).

**Middleware** — `internal/platform/middleware/middleware.go`:
- `RequireCustomerAuth` (customer aud + `app.users` row + optional email-verified gate → `403 email_unverified`) and `RequireAdminAuth` (admin aud + `app.admin_users` row per request → immediate revocation). Wrong-space tokens get `401 invalid_audience` with explicit messaging, including under distinct signing keys (other-space probe on the failure path). Old `RequireAuth`/`RequireAdmin` kept but no longer used by routes.

**Router** — `internal/platform/httpserver/app.go`: three groups wired (`/api/v1/admin/...` → admin chain, `/api/v1/...` orgs/merchant → customer chain with verification enforced, `/api/v1/payments/...` → API-key only). New `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login`, `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/invite`, `GET /api/v1/auth/me`, `GET /api/v1/admin/auth/me`. `GET /api/v1/admin/me` kept as read-only deprecated compat accepting either audience (current frontend keeps working until Phase 4).

**Seed + config**: `cmd/seed-admin` now writes `app.admin_users` (works pre/post-migration, leaves customer rows untouched); `.env.example` documents the four new vars; `AUTH_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET` length-validated.

## Verification
- `go build`, `go vet`: clean. `go test ./...`: all packages pass, including new `audience_test.go` (cross-audience rejection, legacy-token rejection, shared-secret audience enforcement).
- `go test -race`: **not runnable here** (no gcc on this Windows box) — needs CI or a machine with a C toolchain.
- Migration `up` applied to dev DB; `down` round-trip **untested** against live data.

## Decisions you need to make / open items
1. Legacy sessions are revoked (no-`aud` tokens rejected) — confirm acceptable, or ask for a grace alias.
2. Email-verification is now **strictly enforced** on all org/merchant routes (OTP + `/me` stay open). First action after deploy: create admin via seed, then register customer + verify OTP.
3. `ADMIN_EMAILS` in `backend/.env` is now fully dead — remove it.
4. Set a distinct `AUTH_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET` in production.
5. Frontend still uses the single token + deprecated `/admin/me` — Phase 4 replaces it. Until then, admins opening merchant pages with an admin token get `invalid_audience` (expected; merchant UI moves to customer login in Phase 4).

## Assistant

Fixed and verified live, mzee. Two problems, two fixes — committed as `3da31b6`.

## 1. `registration_disabled` — root cause
Your dev backend had no `AUTH_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTER` set, so it defaulted to `false`, and with users already in the table the gate stayed shut. Since admins now come only from `seed-admin` (Phase 1), there is no reason to keep merchant signup closed:
- `backend/internal/platform/config/config.go`: `AUTH_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTER` now **defaults to `true`**. Registration only ever creates customer accounts — never admins.
- Your local `backend/.env` (gitignored): replaced the dead `ADMIN_EMAILS` line with `AUTH_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTER=true`, and I restarted the API with the new build.
- Docs updated: `backend/.env.example`, `backend/README.md`.

## 2. Merchant route naming (frontend)
- **Merchants**: `/login` and `/register` (with `/signin`, `/signup` kept as aliases so bookmarks keep working).
- **Admins**: `/admin/login` — separate page hitting `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login`, operator-only heading, no self-registration toggle.
- Guards redirect correctly now: merchant pages → `/login?next=…`, admin pages → `/admin/login?next=…`.
- New `authenticateAdmin()` in `frontend/src/lib/auth.ts`.

## Verified just now against your running server
- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` → creates merchant, `is_admin: false` (your exact error, gone).
- Customer login → OK; same credentials on `/api/v1/admin/auth/login` → `401`.
- Customer token on `/api/v1/admin/auth/me` → `401 invalid_audience` ("Customer tokens are not accepted here — sign in at /admin/login").
- `go build`, `go vet`, `go test -count=1 ./...` pass; `npm run build` succeeds; migration `000044` down→up round-trip works.

## Notes
- A clearly-named `smoke.merchant@example.com` test account remains in your local dev DB (no `psql` here to remove it) — delete it or leave it, it's harmless.
- I restarted your API (killed old PID, fresh `lipago.exe` build). Restart your frontend dev server (`npm run dev`) to pick up the new routes, then open `http://localhost:5173/register` to sign up a merchant.
- Interim limitation (full split lands in Phase 4): admin and customer sessions still share one browser storage key, so only one space stays signed in at a time.

## Assistant

Imeeleweka, mzee — sasa `/onboarding/create-org` na kurasa zote za merchant zinafunguka upande wa merchant, si admin. Committed.

## Kilichobadilika

**`CustomerLayout` mpya** (`frontend/src/pages/CustomerLayout.tsx`):
- Header ya merchant: logo + beji ya kijani **MERCHANT**, org switcher, nav ya merchant (**My Apps**, **New Organization**), sign-out → `/login`.
- Inaonesha `SandboxModeBanner` (sandbox/KYC) — kama awali.

**`AdminLayout` imesafishwa** (`frontend/src/pages/AdminLayout.tsx`):
- Nav ya admin pekee: Overview, Apps, Withdrawals, Providers, KYC review. Beji nyekundu **ADMIN**.
- Imeondolewa: org switcher, link ya "Merchant", na sandbox banner — vitu vya merchant havionekani tena kwa admin.

**`App.tsx`**: routes zote za merchant (`/merchant/*`, `/onboarding/create-org`, `/onboarding/kyc/:orgId`, `/org/:orgId/*`) sasa zinatumia `CustomerLayout`. Admin (`/admin/*`) inabaki na `AdminLayout`.

## Kujaribu
Anzisha backend (`go run ./cmd/api` ndani ya `backend/`) na frontend (`npm run dev`), kisha fungua `http://localhost:5173/onboarding/create-org` — utaona header ya merchant (MERCHANT badge, My Apps, org switcher), bila nav ya admin.

## Bado (Phase 4 kamili)
- `/` na `*` bado zinaelekeza `/admin/payments` — landing page kulingana na role + 404 kwa customer anayejaribu `/admin` URL zinakuja Phase 4.
- Session key bado ni moja kwa pande zote mbili (kutengwa kamili kwa storage kuja Phase 4).
- Kumbuka: kosa la `tsc` kuhusu `vitest/globals` ni la zamani kwenye repo, halikutokana na mabadiliko haya (`vite build` inapita).

## Assistant

Imekamilika, mzee — committed (`43bc43f`).

## Ufafanuzi muhimu (usichanganye)

- **Apps**: tayari ziko merchant side — `/merchant/apps` (orodha + kutengeneza app) na `/merchant/apps/:id` (webhooks, API keys, deliveries). `/admin/payments/apps` ni mtazamo wa admin wa apps zote عبر organizations zote — merchant hapaswi kuiona, kwa hiyo haijahamishwa. Tumia `/merchant/apps`.
- **Withdrawals**: hizi ndizo zilikuwa admin pekee kwa merchant. Sasa zipo merchant side.

## Kilichoongezwa merchant side
Tab mpya ya **Withdrawals** ndani ya `/merchant/apps/:id`:
- Orodha ya withdrawals za app husika (scoped — merchant anaona za app yake pekee, backend ina-enforce).
- **New withdrawal** dialog: amount (TZS), bank transfer au mobile money, notes.
- **Approve / Reject** kwa withdrawals zilizo `requested` (finance/owner roles, kama backend inavyoruhusu).
- Mark-paid / dispatch bado ni kazi ya admin (upande wa admin) — merchant anaona status (`paid`, `failed`, n.k.) baada ya admin kumaliza.

Backend haikuguswa — endpoints za merchant (`GET/POST /api/v1/merchant/apps/{id}/withdrawals`, `approve`, `reject`) zilikuwepo tayari; frontend ndiyo ilikuwa haijaziunganisha.

## Kujaribu
Fungua `http://localhost:5173/merchant/apps` → chagua app → tab ya **Withdrawals**. Kumbuka backend inahitaji kuwaka (`go run ./cmd/api` ndani ya `backend/`).

## Assistant

Imefunguliwa kwa muda, mzee — committed (`74b93d9`).

## Nini kilikuwa kinakuzuia
Mailer halisi haipo kwenye dev (OTP ni log-only stub), kwa hiyo code ya email haikufika kwako — na gate ya backend ilikataa kuendelea bila `email_verified`. Nimeongeza switch badala ya kuondoa OTP kabisa:

- **`AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION`** (default `true` — production inabaki salama). Kwenye dev `.env` yako nimeweka `false` **kwa muda**.
- OTP endpoints zenyewe bado zipo — zitahitajika tena mailer itakapo-unganishwa.

## Ufanye nini sasa
1. Anzisha backend upya: `cd backend` → `go run ./cmd/api` (lazima i-restart kusoma `.env` mpya).
2. Kwenye ukurasa wa signup, baada ya kuunda account bonyeza **"Skip for now (sandbox only until verified)"** — sasa utaingia moja kwa moja kwenye `/onboarding/create-org` bila kuzuiwa.

## Muhimu
- Hii ni ya dev pekee. Kabla ya test yoyote ya kweli au production: futa mstari `AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false` kwenye `backend/.env`, au weka mailer halisi (SES/SendGrid/Beem) — nitakuunganishia ukiniambia provider gani.
- Build + vet + tests zote zinapita ✓

## Assistant

Imekamilika, mzee — committed (`f730608`).

## Frontend (removed)
- **Leave org button** — imeondolewa kwenye Members page (`OrgMembers.tsx`). Owner bado anaweza kumtoa member mwingine (Remove), lakini hakuna kitufe cha kujiondoa mwenyewe.
- **Org switcher** — imeondolewa kwenye merchant header (`CustomerLayout.tsx`). Header sasa: logo + MERCHANT badge, My Apps, New Organization, sign-out.
- Usafi wa ziada: `SandboxModeBanner` sasa inafuata org yako moja kwa moja (hakuna localStorage lookup), na marejeo ya switcher kwenye CreateOrg/OrgSettings yameondolewa.

## Backend (sheria mpya: one org per account)
- `POST /api/v1/orgs` → ukishakuwa na org hai, unapata **409 `single_org`** ("Each account belongs to a single organization.").
- **Invites + accept** → mtu mwenye org hai hawezi kualikwa wala kukubali mwaliko wa pili (invited-but-unaccepted haihesabiki, check inarudiwa wakati wa accept).
- Endpoint ya `leave` imebaki kimya kimya (owner-removal haijaathirika), na data zilizopo za dev hazijaguswa — sheria inatumika kwa vitendo vipya pekee.

## Uthibitisho
- `go build`, `go vet`, `go test -count=1 ./...` — zote pass, pamoja na test mpya `TestSingleOrgPerAccount`.
- `npm run build` ✓.

Kumbuka kuwasha upya backend (`go run ./cmd/api`) ili sheria mpya ianze kufanya kazi.

  "content": "import { useState } from \"react\";\nimport { Link } from \"react-router-dom\";\nimport { useQueries, useQuery, useQueryClient } from \"@tanstack/react-query\";\nimport { Check, X } from \"lucide-react\";\nimport { Button } from \"@/components/ui/button\";\nimport { Badge } from \"@/components/ui/badge\";\nimport { Card, CardContent } from \"@/components/ui/card\";\nimport { Skeleton } from \"@/components/ui/skeleton\";\nimport { toast } from \"@/components/ui/sonner\";\nimport {\n  approveMerchantWithdrawal,\n  listMerchantWithdrawals,\n  listMyApps,\n  rejectMerchantWithdrawal,\n} from \"@/lib/merchantApi\";\n\nfunction errorMessage(err: unknown, fallback: string) {\n  return err instanceof Error ? err.message : fallback;\n}\n\n// Merchant-space Withdrawals: every payout request across all apps, with\n// approve/reject inline (finance/owner). New requests are created per app\n// under My Apps → Manage → Withdrawals.\nconst MerchantWithdrawals = () => {\n  const queryClient = useQueryClient();\n  const [appFilter, setAppFilter] = useState(\"\");\n  const [actingId, setActingId] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  const appsQuery = useQuery({ queryKey: [\"merchant\", \"my-apps\"], queryFn: () => listMyApps(), staleTime: 30_000 });\n  const apps = appsQuery.data ?? [];\n  const appName = (appId: string) => apps.find((a) => a.id === appId)?.name ?? \"App\";\n\n  const withdrawalQueries = useQueries({\n    queries: apps.map((app) => ({\n      queryKey: [\"merchant\", app.id, \"withdrawals\"],\n      queryFn: () => listMerchantWithdrawals(app.id),\n      staleTime: 15_000,\n    })),\n  });\n  const loading = appsQuery.isLoading || withdrawalQueries.some((q) => q.isLoading);\n\n  const withdrawals = withdrawalQueries.flatMap((q, i) =>\n    (q.data ?? []).map((w) => ({ ...w, app_id: apps[i]?.id ?? w.app_id })),\n  ).filter((w) => !appFilter || w.app_id === appFilter);\n\n  const reload = () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [\"merchant\"] });\n\n  const runAction = async (appId: string, id: string, action: () => Promise<unknown>, successMessage: string) => {\n    setActingId(id);\n    try {\n      await action();\n      toast.success(successMessage);\n      reload();\n    } catch (err) {\n      toast.error(errorMessage(err, \"Unable to update withdrawal.\"));\n    } finally {\n      setActingId(null);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <div>\n        <h2 className=\"text-2xl font-bold text-slate-900\">Withdrawals</h2>\n        <p className=\"mt-1 text-sm text-slate-500\">Payout requests across all your apps. New requests are created per app under My Apps → Manage.</p>\n      </div>\n\n      <div className=\"mt-4 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2\">\n        <select\n          aria-label=\"Filter by app\"\n          className=\"h-9 rounded-md border border-slate-300 px-2 text-sm\"\n          value={appFilter}\n          onChange={(e) => setAppFilter(e.target.value)}\n        >\n          <option value=\"\">All apps</option>\n          {apps.map((a) => (\n            <option key={a.id} value={a.id}>{a.name}</option>\n          ))}\n        </select>\n      </div>\n\n      <div className=\"mt-4 space-y-3\">\n        {loading && <Card><CardContent className=\"p-4\"><Skeleton className=\"h-16 w-full\" /></CardContent></Card>}\n        {!loading && withdrawals.length === 0 && (\n          <Card><CardContent className=\"flex flex-col items-center gap-2 p-10 text-center\">\n            <p className=\"text-sm font-medium text-slate-600\">No withdrawals yet.</p>\n          </CardContent></Card>\n        )}\n        {withdrawals.map((w) => {\n          const busy = actingId === w.id;\n          return (\n            <Card key={`${w.app_id}-${w.id}`}>\n              <CardContent className=\"flex flex-col gap-3 p-4 sm:flex-row sm:items-start sm:justify-between\">\n                <div className=\"min-w-0\">\n                  <div className=\"flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2\">\n                    <Link to={`/merchant/apps/${w.app_id}`} className=\"text-sm font-semibold text-blue-600 hover:underline\">\n                      {appName(w.app_id)}\n                    </Link>\n                    <Badge variant=\"outline\">{w.status}</Badge>\n                  </div>\n                  <p className=\"mt-1 text-lg font-extrabold text-slate-900\">{w.amount} {w.currency}</p>\n                  <p className=\"mt-1 text-xs text-slate-400\">Requested {w.created_at ? new Date(w.created_at).toLocaleString() : \"—\"}</p>\n                  {w.notes && <p className=\"mt-1 text-xs text-slate-500\">Note: {w.notes}</p>}\n                </div>\n                {w.status === \"requested\" && (\n                  <div className=\"flex shrink-0 flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5 self-end sm:self-start\">\n                    <Button size=\"sm\" disabled={busy} onClick={() => runAction(w.app_id, w.id, () => approveMerchantWithdrawal(w.app_id, w.id), \"Withdrawal approved — balance debited.\")}>\n                      <Check className=\"h-3.5 w-3.5 mr-1\" /> Approve\n                    </Button>\n                    <Button size=\"sm\" variant=\"outline\" disabled={busy} onClick={() => runAction(w.app_id, w.id, () => rejectMerchantWithdrawal(w.app_id, w.id), \"Withdrawal rejected.\")}>\n                      <X className=\"h-3.5 w-3.5 mr-1\" /> Reject\n                    </Button>\n                  </div>\n                )}\n              </CardContent>\n            </Card>\n          );\n        })}\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n};\n\nexport default MerchantWithdrawals;\n",

## Navigation mpya (merchant)
**My Apps · Payments · Withdrawals · Webhooks · API Keys · Deliveries · Settings**

- **Payments** (`/merchant/payments`) — orders zote kwa apps zako zote, na filter ya app + status. Kila mstari una link kwenda app husika.
- **Withdrawals** (`/merchant/withdrawals`) — payouts zote kwa apps zote, na **Approve/Reject moja kwa moja** hapo hapo (finance/owner). Kuunda mpya bado ni per-app (My Apps → Manage).
- **Webhooks** — endpoints zote: URL, events, status, secret version.
- **API Keys** — prefixes zote: label, environment (live/sandbox badge), status, tarehe.
- **Deliveries** — deliveries zote na filter ya app + status.
- **Settings** — inakupeleka moja kwa moja kwenye settings za organization yako (one org per account, hakuna kuchagua).

## Muhimu
- Kila ukurasa una **filter ya app**, kwa hiyo bado unaweza kuona kitu cha app moja ukitaka.
- Backend haikuguswa — kurasa zinachanganya tu data ambazo account yako tayari inaruhusiwa kuona (membership-scoped, kama awali).
- Usimamizi wa kina (kutengeneza keys/endpoints, replay deliveries) unabaki per-app chini ya My Apps → Manage.

## User

ROLE
You are a senior Go + React engineer working in dadyutenga/payment-gateway
(LipaGO). Build out the merchant Settings page for the customer space.
Start by reading, then plan, then build. Do not change unrelated pages.

Repo layout: Go backend in backend/ (internal/modules/..., migrations/),
React frontend (locate it, read its router, layouts, API client, auth
context and existing component/styling conventions first).

PHASE 0 - STUDY (read-only, report before coding)
1. Find the current page at /org/:orgId/settings. List what it renders and
   which endpoints it calls today (org name, business name, verification
   card, delete org).
2. Read: organizations, org_members, kyc_submissions, org limits/fee
   override tables, api keys, webhook endpoints, notification/mailer/SMS
   interfaces, audit_log, file upload code. Say what exists, what is
   stubbed, what is missing.
3. Read the role permission definitions (owner/finance/developer/viewer)
   and how middleware resolves org_id and role from the session.
4. Post a short plan: migrations needed, endpoints to add, components to
   add. Wait for my go-ahead only if something is ambiguous or risky;
   otherwise continue.

TARGET: Settings page with tabs or sections
Use a tabbed layout (General, Verification, Limits & Fees, Security,
Notifications, Branding, Payouts, Danger zone). Keep the existing look
and the LipaGO MERCHANT header. Each tab loads its own data so the page
stays fast.

1) GENERAL
- Fields: Organization name, Business name (helper text under each
  explaining the difference: org name is the workspace label, business
  name is the legal/trading name shown to customers and used for KYC).
- Read-only Org ID with a copy button.
- Business details: TIN, business address, business phone, contact email.
  After KYC is verified, TIN and business name become read-only and show
  "Changing this requires re-verification" with a "Request change"
  button that opens a KYC resubmission.
- Save button uses the primary brand color (NOT red), disabled until the
  form is dirty, shows loading and success/error states.
- Permissions: owner can edit; other roles see read-only fields.

2) VERIFICATION (KYC)
- Status card with real states: pending, submitted, verified, rejected.
  Icons and colors: verified = green check, submitted = blue clock,
  pending = amber, rejected = red with the admin's rejection reason.
  (The current UI shows an amber warning shield even when verified; fix
  that.)
- Buttons: "Submit verification" (pending), "Resubmit" (rejected), none
  when verified or submitted.
- Submission form: business name, TIN, ID document upload (image or PDF,
  size limit, stored privately, served only via an authenticated
