# Phase 0 Report — merchant Settings page (read-only, no code changed)

## 1. Current `/org/:orgId/settings` (`frontend/src/pages/OrgSettings.tsx`)
- Verification card (`:82-105`): **always amber `ShieldAlert`** regardless of status — confirms your reported bug. Copy per status exists (`KYC_COPY`, `:17-22`). Link to `/onboarding/kyc/:orgId` hidden when verified (`:99`).
- Live limits shown as text (`:91-96`, from `org.live_max_txn_amount/live_daily_volume_cap`), "Ask an admin to adjust them."
- Name/business-name form, owner-only (`:107-127`); Save always enabled (not dirty-tracked), no Org ID row, no TIN/address/phone fields.
- Delete org button sits **inside the same form card** (`:119-122`), outline-styled, not red.
- Endpoints used: `GET/PATCH /api/v1/orgs/:id` (`orgApi.ts:132-138`), `DELETE /api/v1/orgs/:id` (`:140-142`). Backend `UpdateOrganization` accepts **name + business_name only** (`orgs/service.go:109-125`, `repository.go:220-234`).

## 2. What exists / stubbed / missing
| Area | State |
|---|---|
| `organizations` table | `000035`: name, slug, kyc_status, business_name, tin + `000043` live-limit overrides. **No** address/phone/contact-email/branding columns. TIN exists but nothing reads/writes it except KYC submit (`repository.go:490-494` writes business_name+tin on submit). |
| `org_members`, roles | Matrix single-sourced in `orgs/model.go:44-57`; always resolved server-side (`CheckOrgPermission`). No changes needed. |
| `kyc_submissions` | **One row per org, upsert on resubmit** (`repository.go:476-489`, review fields cleared) — **no history**. "View previous submissions" needs a new `kyc_submission_attempts` table. Document upload: JPEG/PNG/WEBP/PDF, 5MB, `uploads/kyc/`, authed endpoints only (`orgs/handler.go:287-440`). Real, not stubbed. |
| Limits usage | `TodayLiveVolume(appID, currency)` exists (`payments/repository.go:2799-2813`, live env only, ledger-sourced, uncached) but **per-app**; no org-level endpoint. Daily caps are per-app per-currency. |
| Fees | Per-**app** fees only (`fee_type/percent/fixed`). **No per-org fee override** anywhere. Merchant display = read each app's fee. |
| Password change | **No endpoint.** Auth has register/login/OTP only. Also no session table (single Bearer token) → no "active sessions" list without a new table. |
| Notifications | `Mailer`/`SMSSender` are **log-only stubs** (`auth.go:506-533`); notify/audit interfaces unwired except admin-login audit rows. No prefs storage. |
| Branding, saved payout destinations | **Nothing** — no columns, no tables. |
| `audit_log` table | Exists (`000044`); only admin-login events written. No org-settings audit. |

## 3. Plan (numbered)
1. **Migration `000045_org_settings`**: `organizations` += `address, phone, contact_email, logo_url, primary_color` (nullable); new `kyc_submission_attempts` (org, evidence snapshot, status, reason, reviewed_by/at, timestamps; written on every submit/decide, `kyc_submissions` stays the live row); new `notification_prefs` (org PK, per-event booleans). No FK breaks; down migration drops them.
2. **Backend**: extend `PATCH /orgs/:id` (new profile fields; TIN+business_name locked once verified → `409 reverification_required` + "Request change" = resubmit KYC which unlocks on submit); `GET /orgs/:id/limits-usage` (effective caps: org override else platform default, today's live volume per app/currency via existing query, per-app fees); `GET /orgs/:id/kyc/attempts` (history); `POST /api/v1/auth/password` (change password); audit row on org-profile changes. All behind existing `RequireCustomerAuth` + `CheckOrgPermission` (owner for writes).
3. **Frontend**: rewrite `OrgSettings.tsx` into tabbed layout (Tabs component already used in `MerchantAppDetail.tsx`) — General, Verification, Limits & Fees, Security, Notifications, Branding, Payouts, Danger zone — each tab its own react-query fetch; fix status icons (green/blue/amber/red); dirty-tracked brand-color Save; read-only Org ID + copy; red Danger zone with delete moved there.

## Settings mpya — tabs 8 (`/org/:id/settings`)
- **General**: org name (workspace label helper), business name (legal/trading helper), Org ID + copy, TIN, address, phone, contact email. Save inafanya kazi dirty-tracked na rangi ya brand (si red). Owner-only edit; wengine read-only. TIN + business name zinalock baada ya verified — "Request change" inaelekea resubmission.
- **Verification**: status card yenye rangi sahihi (green check / blue clock / amber / red + admin rejection reason — amber Herkunft bug imekwisha), Submit/Resubmit buttons kwa owner, na **submission history** yenye tarehe na maamuzi.
- **Limits & Fees** (read-only): caps halisi (org override vs platform default), today's live volume na progress bar kwa kila app/currency, na fee inayotumika kwa kila app.
- **Security**: change password (current + new 12+ chars) — kila member anabadilisha yake.
- **Notifications**: toggles 5 (payments, refunds, expiries, withdrawals, KYC) — zinahifadhiwa DB; delivery bado log-only hadi provider aunganishwe.

## Logo upload moja kwa moja (Branding tab)
- **Upload logo** file picker: JPEG/PNG/WebP, chini ya 2MB (ina-checked pia browser side kabla ya kutuma).
- **…or paste a logo URL** bado ipo kama mbadala.
- Preview inaonyesha logo halisi mara tu inapopakiwa.

## Usalama (kama KYC docs)
- `POST /api/v1/orgs/:id/logo` (owner/manage_org), `GET /api/v1/orgs/:id/logo` (member yeyote wa org) — zote nyuma ya customer auth.
- Content-sniffed (si extension pekee), **SVG imezuiwa makusudi** (stored-XSS), PDF hairuhusiwi.
- Hifadhi ya private `uploads/branding/` (`0750/0640`), path confinement dhidi ya `..` escape — hakuna public URL.
- URL za nje (`http…`) zina-redirect; chochote kingine ni 404.

## Imepimwa live
Upload ya PNG → `stored as: uploads/branding/<org>-<nano>.png` → GET inarudisha `image/png, 70 bytes` ✓. `go build/vet/test` ✓, `vite build` ✓, backend inawaka na routes mpya.

## Admin home dashboard (`/admin`)
Kama ya merchant — makadi na counts halisi:
- **Customers, Organizations, Apps, KYC awaiting review, Operators, Withdrawals requested** — kila kadi na link kwenda sehemu husika.
- **Organizations by verification** (pending/submitted/verified/rejected).
- **Withdrawals by status**.
- **KYC queue table** (5 za kwanza) na link kwenda review.

## Backend: `GET /api/v1/admin/stats`
Endpoint mpya (admin-only) — counts kutoka DB moja kwa moja. Imepimwa live: `{customers:4, admins:2, organizations:3, apps:4, withdrawals:{...}}` ✓. Customer token inakataliwa na `invalid_audience` ✓.

## Bonus fix muhimu
`seed-admin` **haikufanya kazi kabisa** — ilikuwa inatupa `ping postgres: context deadline exceeded` kwa sababu pool iliundwa bila timeouts (`HealthTimeout: 0` = deadline ya papo hapo). Nimerekebisha, na sasa `go run ./cmd/seed-admin -email ops@example.com` inafanya kazi (nimetengeneza admin huyo kwenye dev DB yako — password uliyonipa haijahifadhiwa popote kwenye repo).

## User

MEGA PROMPT - Phase 2: Analytics (Admin + Merchant)
Repo: dadyutenga/payment-gateway (LipaGO)
Backend: Go, backend/ (internal/modules/..., cmd/api, cmd/worker,
migrations/). Frontend: React (locate the app, read its router, layouts,
API client, auth contexts and chart/table conventions first).

Two spaces already exist and MUST stay separated:
- Admin space:    /admin/...  , API group /api/v1/admin/...  (aud=admin)
- Customer space: /org/:orgId/..., API group /api/v1/... (aud=customer,
  org-scoped)
Analytics endpoints follow the same partition. A customer can never see
another org's numbers, and no platform-wide number is ever exposed to
customers.

Work in blocks. Finish each (migration + backend + frontend + tests)
before starting the next. Report after each block.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCK 0 - STUDY (read-only, report before coding)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. Inventory the data available for analytics, with file/line refs:
   orders (status set, provider, amount, currency, fee, environment,
   created_at, paid/settled timestamps, failure reason/code, payer
   phone or identifier, expiry), ledger entries (types, environment),
   withdrawals (status, timestamps), webhook events and deliveries
   (status, attempts, timestamps), reconciliation state, orgs (created_at,
   kyc_status, suspended), apps, api keys (last_used_at).
2. For each metric below, say whether it can be computed TODAY, needs a
   new column, or needs a new table. Examples of likely gaps:
   time-to-pay needs a reliable paid_at; failure reasons need a stored
   normalized reason code; abandonment needs order expiry (expired
   status); repeat-customer rate needs a hashed payer identifier;
   latency per provider needs provider request/response timing stored
   at call time; payment-method mix needs a stored channel/network.
3. Check existing indexes on the hot columns (created_at, org_id, app_id,
   provider, status, environment) and the size assumptions (rows/day).
4. Post a plan: gaps, migrations, rollup strategy, endpoint list, page
   list. Continue unless something is ambiguous or risky.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCK 1 - DATA FOUNDATION (shared by both sides)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Metric definitions (write these into docs/ANALYTICS.md and use them
consistently everywhere):
- TPV: sum of successful payment amounts (gross), per currency, never
  summed across currencies.
- Revenue: sum of platform fees on successful payments, minus fee
  refunds if refunds return fees.
- Success rate: succeeded / (succeeded + failed + expired). Show
  pending separately and exclude it from the denominator.
- Abandonment rate: expired (or never-completed) / created.
- Average time to pay: median and p90 of (paid_at - created_at) for
  succeeded orders. Prefer median and percentiles over plain averages.
- Provider latency: median and p95 of provider API round trip and of
  time-to-confirmation, per provider.
- Repeat-customer rate: payers with 2+ successful payments in the period
  / payers with 1+ (use a hashed payer identifier, see privacy below).
- Churn risk: define transparently, e.g. an active merchant whose 14-day
  volume dropped more than X% versus the prior 14 days, or no
  transactions for N days after a previously steady pattern. Keep
  thresholds configurable and show WHY a merchant is flagged.
- Dormant: verified org with zero successful live transactions in the
  last N days (configurable, default 30).
Rules for every metric: environment = live only by default, with an
explicit sandbox toggle for merchants; sandbox data NEVER mixes into
platform-wide admin numbers. Time bucketing uses Africa/Dar_es_Salaam
(EAT) and states the timezone in the API response.

Data changes (new migrations only, sequential, up/down, never edit old
ones), only for gaps found in Block 0, for example:
- orders: paid_at, failure_code (normalized enum), failure_message,
  channel/network, payer_hash (HMAC of phone with a server secret, never
  the raw number in analytics tables), provider_latency_ms.
- Indexes: (org_id, environment, created_at), (app_id, created_at),
  (provider, status, created_at), partial index on status IN
  (pending, processing) for ops queries.
- Rollup tables refreshed by the worker (reuse the existing worker loop
  and SKIP LOCKED pattern), for example:
    analytics_daily_app  (day, org_id, app_id, environment, provider,
                          channel, currency, created, succeeded, failed,
                          expired, gross, fees, refunds, p50_ttp_s, p90_ttp_s)
    analytics_hourly_app (hour bucket, same dimensions, counts only)
  Rollups are a cache: rebuildable from orders/ledger at any time. Add a
  `cmd/backfill-analytics` (or worker flag) to rebuild a date range, and
  make refresh idempotent (upsert by natural key).
- Query strategy: use rollups for date ranges beyond the current day and
  live queries for "today" and for ops/exception views that must be
  real-time. Money totals shown on statements/exports are computed from
  the LEDGER, not from rollups.
- Add short TTL caching (in-process) for expensive dashboard calls,
  keyed by scope, with clear invalidation by time only.

Tests: metric definitions against a fixture dataset with known answers
(including expired, refunded, mixed currencies, sandbox rows that must be
excluded, timezone day boundaries), rollup rebuild equals live query.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCK 2 - ADMIN ANALYTICS (backend)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
All under /api/v1/admin/analytics/..., admin auth only, every request
read-only. Common query params: from, to, granularity
(hour/day/week/month), provider, currency, org_id (optional filter).

Endpoints:
1. GET /overview  -> TPV, revenue, tx count, success rate, abandonment
   rate, median/p90 time to pay, active merchants, new signups, with
   previous-period comparison (delta and % change) and a time series.
2. GET /providers -> per provider: volume, count, success rate, failure
   breakdown, median/p95 latency, uptime-ish signal (recent failure
   streaks), revenue, plus channel/network split (M-Pesa, Airtel, Tigo,
   others as they exist in the data).
3. GET /merchants/top -> top orgs by TPV and by revenue, with trend,
   success rate, refund rate. Pagination and sort.
4. GET /merchants/signups -> new orgs over time, funnel:
   registered -> email verified -> org created -> KYC submitted ->
   KYC verified -> first live transaction, with conversion and median
   time between steps.
5. GET /merchants/dormant and GET /merchants/churn-risk -> lists with the
   reason each is flagged, last transaction date, 14-day trend, contact
   email, link to org detail. Thresholds from config.
6. GET /failures -> failure reasons ranked (normalized code + provider),
   trend, affected merchants, sample order ids.
7. GET /withdrawals -> pending withdrawals count and amount, AGING
   buckets (<1h, 1-6h, 6-24h, 1-3d, >3d), failed payouts, approval queue
   size (four-eyes), average time to pay out.
8. GET /webhooks -> delivery health: success rate, retry rate, p95
   delivery latency, endpoints failing repeatedly (top offenders with
   consecutive failures), deliveries stuck in processing beyond N min.
9. GET /ops/stuck-orders -> orders pending/processing longer than N
   minutes, by provider, with age and org.
10. GET /ops/unreconciled -> paid-at-provider-but-not-in-ledger and
   ledger-but-not-confirmed mismatches, age, amount.
11. GET /ops/negative-balances -> orgs whose available or ledger balance
   is below zero, with the entries that caused it.
12. GET /export/:report?format=csv -> CSV for any of the above lists.
Every admin analytics call is written to the audit log only for exports
(reads are not audited, exports are, since they can carry merchant data).

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCK 3 - ADMIN ANALYTICS (frontend)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Inside AdminLayout, new pages:
- /admin/analytics (Overview): KPI cards (TPV, revenue, success rate,
  median time to pay, active merchants, signups) each with delta vs
  previous period; date range picker with presets (today, 7d, 30d, MTD,
  custom); line/area chart for volume and revenue; bar for tx count;
  success-rate trend.
- /admin/analytics/providers: table + charts per provider (volume share,
  success rate, latency p50/p95 over time); network split.
- /admin/analytics/merchants: tabs Top, Signups funnel, Dormant, Churn
  risk. Rows link to /admin/orgs/:orgId. Churn/dormant rows show the
  reason and a "copy contact email" action.
- /admin/analytics/failures: ranked reasons with drill-down to sample
  orders.
- /admin/ops: cards and tables for stuck orders, unreconciled payments,
  negative balances, pending withdrawal aging, webhook health, each with
  a count badge and an auto-refresh (30-60s) toggle. Red/amber/green
  thresholds configurable.
- Every table: sortable, paginated, CSV export button, empty and error
  states. Every chart: tooltip, accessible labels, not color-only.
Use the chart library already in the repo; if none, add one lightweight
option and say why (prefer recharts if the stack is React).

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCK 4 - MERCHANT ANALYTICS (backend)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Under the customer API group, org-scoped and app-scoped. Org and role
resolved server-side from the session, NEVER from client params. Roles:
owner, finance, developer, viewer can read analytics; finance and owner
can export settlement statements; developers see operational metrics but
not payer-level detail. Query params: app_id (optional, must belong to
the org), environment (live default, sandbox toggle), from, to,
granularity, currency.

Endpoints:
1. GET /orgs/:orgId/analytics/overview -> revenue (net of fees and
   refunds), gross volume, tx count, success rate, abandonment rate,
   median time to pay, avg order value, with previous-period deltas and
   time series.
2. GET /orgs/:orgId/analytics/methods -> payment-method/network mix
   (M-Pesa, Airtel, Tigo, etc.) with count, volume, success rate.
3. GET /orgs/:orgId/analytics/peak-hours -> heatmap data by weekday x
   hour in EAT, plus best/worst hours.
4. GET /orgs/:orgId/analytics/customers -> repeat-customer rate, new vs
   returning payers over time, top payers by count/volume shown ONLY as
   masked identifiers (e.g. +255 7** *** 123), never the full number.
5. GET /orgs/:orgId/analytics/failures -> failure reasons for this org
   with human-readable explanations and suggested actions (e.g. insufficient
   funds, wrong PIN, timeout, network unavailable).
6. GET /orgs/:orgId/analytics/apps -> per-app comparison table.
7. Settlement statements (ledger-based, never from rollups):
   GET /orgs/:orgId/settlements?from&to&app_id -> gross, fees, refunds,
   net settled, per-provider breakdown, itemized entries, opening and
   closing balance, currency. Exports: format=csv (stdlib encoding/csv)
   and format=pdf (use a library already in go.mod, otherwise the lightest
   maintained PDF lib, and say why) with letterhead: org business name,
   period, generated at (EAT), statement id, summary totals, itemized
   table, page numbers. Statement totals must equal the ledger sum for
   the period; add a test asserting it.
8. Exports are rate-limited, audit-logged, and generated async if large
   (background job + download link that requires auth and expires).

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCK 5 - MERCHANT ANALYTICS (frontend)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Inside CustomerLayout, new pages under /org/:orgId/:
- /analytics (Overview): KPI cards with deltas, revenue-over-time chart,

- /analytics/methods: payment-method mix donut/bars + table.
- /analytics/peak-hours: weekday x hour heatmap with a plain-language

- /analytics/customers: repeat rate, new vs returning chart, masked top

- /analytics/failures: reasons with plain explanations and suggested

- /settlements: list of periods with download buttons (CSV, PDF), custom

- Add "Analytics" and "Settlements" to the top nav (currently: My Apps,

- Role-aware UI: viewers cannot export; developers do not see payer-level
  data. Never rely on UI hiding for security.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCK 6 - PRIVACY, PERFORMANCE, SECURITY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
- Payer phone numbers: analytics uses payer_hash only. Any masked display
  is derived server-side. Raw numbers never leave the orders/ledger
  tables and never appear in rollups, exports for merchants beyond what
  they already own, or admin analytics.
- Cross-tenant isolation tests on EVERY merchant endpoint (org A cannot
  read org B, app from another org rejected, crafted params ignored).
- Admin/customer partition tests: customer token rejected on every
  /admin/analytics route and admin token rejected on customer routes.
- Query performance: EXPLAIN the top queries on a seeded dataset (write a
  seed tool for e.g. 1-5 million orders across 200 orgs) and show results

## 2. Per-metric verdicts
| Metric | Verdict |
|---|---|
| TPV, revenue (net of fee refunds), success/abandonment rate, avg order value | **Computable TODAY** (orders + status_history + ledger) |
| Median/p90 time-to-pay | **Computable TODAY** via status_history (no new column; `paid_at` derivable — I will NOT add a redundant column) |
| Failure reasons | **NEW column needed**: `failure_code` (normalized enum) + `failure_message` on orders. Today only free-text `events.error` / withdrawal `failure_reason` exist |
| Channel/network mix (M-Pesa/Airtel/Tigo) | **NEW column needed**: `channel` on orders. SonicPesa payloads carry `"channel":"AIRTELMONEY"` (`sonicpesa_test.go:49`) but it is **never stored** |
| Repeat-customer rate | **NEW column needed**: `payer_hash` (HMAC-SHA256 of normalized phone with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`-derived secret, backfilled by one UPDATE). Raw `buyer_phone` must never enter analytics tables/exports |
| Provider latency (API round-trip + time-to-confirm) | **NEW columns needed**: `provider_latency_ms` on orders (round-trip, measured in adapter) + time-to-confirm derivable from status_history vs first provider interaction. Nothing timing-related is stored today |
| Peak-hours heatmap | Computable today (created_at + EAT bucketing) |
| Dormant/churn, signups funnel, stuck orders, negative balances, withdrawal aging | Computable today (orgs + orders + withdrawals + KYC attempts table from migration 000045) |
| Settlements (ledger-based) | Computable today; PDF needs a lib (nothing in `go.mod`) |

34: 		slog.Error("worker config load failed", "error", err)
35: 		os.Exit(1)
36: 	}
37:
38: 	logger := observability.NewLogger(cfg.App)
39: 	slog.SetDefault(logger)
40: 	logger.Info("starting lipago payment system worker", "env", cfg.App.Env)

43: 	if err != nil {

45: 		os.Exit(1)
46: 	}

48:

50: 	if err != nil {

52: 		os.Exit(1)
53: 	}

56: 	paymentService := payments.NewService(paymentRepo, providers.Registry, cipher, payments.ServiceOptions{
57: 		DeliverySigningSecret:          cfg.Payments.DeliverySigningSecret,
58: 		DeliveryTimeout:                cfg.Payments.DeliveryTimeout,
59: 		DeliveryMaxAttempts:            cfg.Payments.DeliveryMaxAttempts,
60: 		ReconciliationStaleAfter:       cfg.Payments.ReconciliationStaleAfter,
61: 		ReconciliationBatchSize:        cfg.Payments.ReconciliationBatchSize,
62: 		AutomatedPayoutsEnabled:        cfg.Payments.AutomatedPayoutsEnabled,
63: 		PayoutProvider:                 cfg.Payments.PayoutProvider,
64: 		PayoutReconciliationStaleAfter: cfg.Payments.PayoutReconciliationStaleAfter,
65: 		ProviderTimeout:                positiveDuration(cfg.HTTP.RequestTimeout-5*time.Second, 10*time.Second),
66: 		OrderExpiryTTL:                 cfg.Payments.OrderTTL,
67: 	}, logger)

69: 	deliveryTicker := time.NewTicker(positiveDuration(cfg.Payments.DeliveryPollInterval, 30*time.Second))
70: 	defer deliveryTicker.Stop()
71: 	reconciliationTicker := time.NewTicker(positiveDuration(cfg.Payments.ReconciliationInterval, 5*time.Minute))
72: 	defer reconciliationTicker.Stop()
73: 	payoutTicker := time.NewTicker(positiveDuration(cfg.Payments.PayoutReconciliationInterval, 5*time.Minute))
74: 	defer payoutTicker.Stop()
75: 	expiryTicker := time.NewTicker(positiveDuration(cfg.Payments.ExpiryInterval, time.Minute))
76: 	defer expiryTicker.Stop()
77:
78: 	processDeliveries := func() {
79: 		result, err := paymentService.ProcessDueDeliveries(ctx, positiveInt(cfg.Payments.DeliveryBatchSize, 25))
80: 		if err != nil {
81: 			logger.Error("payment delivery processing failed", "error", err)
82: 			return
83: 		}
84: 		if result.Claimed > 0 {
85: 			logger.Info("payment deliveries processed", "claimed", result.Claimed, "delivered", result.Delivered, "retrying", result.Retrying, "failed", result.Failed)
86: 		}
87: 	}
88: 	reconcilePayments := func() {
89: 		result, err := paymentService.ReconcilePayments(ctx, positiveInt(cfg.Payments.ReconciliationBatchSize, 50))
90: 		if err != nil {

92: 			return
93: 		}
94: 		if result.Scanned > 0 {
95: 			logger.Info("payment reconciliation completed", "scanned", result.Scanned, "updated", result.Updated)
96: 		}
97: 	}

100: 			return
101: 		}

103: 		if err != nil {
104: 			logger.Error("payout reconciliation failed", "error", err)
105: 			return
106: 		}
107: 		if result.Scanned > 0 {
108: 			logger.Info("payout reconciliation completed", "scanned", result.Scanned, "updated", result.Updated)
109: 		}
110: 	}
111: 	expireOrders := func() {
112: 		result, err := paymentService.ExpireOrders(ctx, positiveInt(cfg.Payments.ReconciliationBatchSize, 50))
113: 		if err != nil {
114: 			logger.Error("payment expiry failed", "error", err)
115: 			return
116: 		}
117: 		if result.Expired > 0 {
118: 			logger.Info("payment expiry completed", "expired", result.Expired)
119: 		}
120: 		if swept, err := paymentService.CleanupIdempotencyKeys(ctx); err != nil {
121: 			logger.Error("idempotency cleanup failed", "error", err)
122: 		} else if swept > 0 {
123: 			logger.Info("idempotency cleanup completed", "deleted", swept)
124: 		}
125: 	}
126:
127: 	processDeliveries()
128: 	reconcilePayments()
129: 	reconcilePayouts()
130: 	expireOrders()
131:
132: 	for {
133: 		select {
134: 		case <-ctx.Done():
135: 			logger.Info("worker stopped cleanly")
136: 			return
137: 		case <-deliveryTicker.C:
138: 			processDeliveries()
139: 		case <-reconciliationTicker.C:
140: 			reconcilePayments()
141: 		case <-payoutTicker.C:
142: 			reconcilePayouts()
143: 		case <-expiryTicker.C:
144: 			expireOrders()
145: 		}
146: 	}
147: }

149: func positiveDuration(value, fallback time.Duration) time.Duration {

152: 	}
153: 	return value
154: }

{
  "content": "# LipaGO Analytics — metric definitions\n\nSingle source of truth for every number on the admin and merchant\ndashboards. All analytics code (SQL, rollups, frontend) MUST match these\ndefinitions. Timezone is **Africa/Dar_es_Salaam (EAT)** everywhere a day\nor hour bucket appears; API responses state the timezone.\n\n## Base filters\n\n- **Environment: live only by default.** Merchants get an explicit\n  sandbox toggle; sandbox rows NEVER mix into platform-wide admin\n  numbers or into live merchant numbers.\n- **Currency is never summed across currencies.** Every money metric is\n  reported per currency.\n\n## Definitions\n\n- **TPV**: sum of `amount` over orders with `status = 'paid'` (gross),\n  per currency.\n- **Revenue**: sum of `platform_fee_debit` ledger entries minus\n  `refund_fee_reversal_credit` entries (fees are NOT kept on refunded\n  money), per currency, over the period.\n- **Success rate**: `paid / (paid + failed + cancelled + reversed +\n  expired)`. `pending`/`processing` are shown separately and EXCLUDED\n  from the denominator.\n- **Abandonment rate**: `expired / created`.\n- **Time to pay**: `first paid transition (status_history) − created_at`\n  over paid orders. Report **median (p50) and p90**, never a plain mean.\n- **Provider latency**: round-trip ms of provider API calls\n  (`provider_latency_ms`, measured around create/status calls);\n  report **median and p95 per provider**. Time-to-confirmation is the\n  time-to-pay distribution sliced per provider.\n- **Repeat-customer rate**: payers with 2+ paid orders in the period /\n  payers with 1+ paid orders, keyed by `payer_hash`\n  (HMAC-SHA256 of the normalized phone, keyed by `ANALYTICS_PAYER_SECRET`;\n  raw numbers never enter analytics). Normalization: digits only,\n  Tanzanian `0…` rewritten to `255…`.\n- **Dormant**: verified org with zero paid live orders in the last N days\n  (default 30, configurable).\n- **Churn risk**: active merchant whose trailing-14-day live volume\n  dropped more than X% (default 50, configurable) versus the prior\n  14 days, OR no transactions for N days after a previously steady\n  pattern. Every flag shows WHY (the two windows and the drop %).\n- **Signup funnel**: registered → email verified → org created → KYC\n  submitted → KYC verified → first live transaction, with conversion\n  and median time between steps.\n\n## Failure codes (`failure_code` enum)\n\n`expired` (TTL, no money moved) · `cancelled` · `provider_declined`\n(provider said no; `failure_message` carries their status text) ·\n`timeout` (provider call deadline) · `system_error` (anything else).\nStamped at final transitions only; expiry stamps in SQL, the rest in\n`applyProviderStatusUpdate`/webhook/create paths. Best-effort: analytics\nstamps never fail money writes.\n\n## Channels (`channel` enum)\n\n`M-PESA | AIRTEL | TIGO | HALOPESA | OTHER`, extracted from provider\nresponses/webhooks (`channel/network/...` keys). Unrecognized non-empty\ninput → `OTHER`; empty → NULL (untouched).\n\n## Rollups (cache, rebuildable)\n\n- `analytics_daily_app(day, org, app, env, provider, channel, currency)`:\n  created/succeeded/failed(expired split out)/expired, gross, p50/p90 TTP.\n- `analytics_daily_app_money(day, org, app, currency)`: fees, refunds,\n  refund_total — separate grain so fees can never double-count across\n  provider/channel rows.\n- `analytics_hourly_app(hour, org, app, env)`: counts only.\n- Refresh: whole EAT days, delete+insert in one transaction (idempotent).\n  Worker refreshes yesterday+today every reconciliation tick; use rollups\n  for ranges beyond today, live queries for today + ops views.\n- **Statements/exports money totals come from the LEDGER, never rollups.**\n- Rebuild: `go run ./cmd/backfill-analytics -from YYYY-MM-DD -to\n  YYYY-MM-DD [-payer-hash-backfill]`. Back up `payment_orders` first\n  (`pg_dump -t app.payment_orders`); refresh itself only writes the\n  `analytics_*` tables.\n\n## Privacy\n\n- Raw payer phones live only in `payment_orders.buyer_phone`.\n- Analytics, rollups, exports, and masked displays use `payer_hash` or\n  server-side masking (`+255 7** *** 123`); full numbers never appear.\n- Merchant endpoints are org-scoped server-side; developers see\n  operational metrics but no payer-level detail.\n\n## Config\n\n`ANALYTICS_PAYER_SECRET` (falls back to the delivery signing secret in\ndev; set distinctly in production) · thresholds live with each endpoint\n(Block 2/4) and are stated in responses.\n",

## Assistant

# Phase 2 BLOCK 2 REPORT — done, committed (`06dc9ef`), pushed ✓

## What changed
New module `backend/internal/modules/analytics/` (model/repository/service/handler, matching repo conventions) + 13 routes in `app.go`, all `RequireAdminAuth`, all read-only:
- `GET /overview` — TPV/revenue (per currency, fees net of fee refunds from ledger), tx count, success/abandonment, median/p90 TTP, active merchants, signups, previous-period % deltas, EAT time series.
- `GET /providers` — volume/count/success/failure codes/median-p95 latency/1h-24h failure signals/channel split/revenue per provider.
- `GET /merchants/top` (`sort`, pagination; TPV/revenue sort in requested currency, default TZS; count-based trend) and `GET /merchants/signups` (funnel series + totals + median hours between steps).
- `GET /merchants/dormant` (verified + no paid live in N days, default 30) and `/merchants/churn-risk` (count-drop >50% default, prior ≥5 to cut noise, reason strings + owner contact).
- `GET /failures` (ranked codes + affected orgs + sample order ids), `/withdrawals` (pending/approval queue/aging buckets/failed/avg payout hours), `/webhooks` (success/retry/p95/stuck/offenders).
- `GET /ops/stuck-orders|unreconciled|negative-balances` (capped 200) and `GET /export/:report?format=csv` (10 reports, attachment download, **audited** to `audit_log`; reads not audited).

## Verified
- `go build/vet` clean; `go test ./...` all pass (incl. new params tests).
- **All 12 data endpoints + export hit live**: 9 passed first try; 3 SQL bugs found and fixed (placeholder collision, funnel GROUP BY, correlated-subquery grouping).
- Export returns `text/csv` attachment; customer token on analytics → `invalid_audience`.

## Untested / notes
- `go test -race`: no gcc here.
- Perf Block 6 will decide if hot endpoints move to rollups (currently live-SQL, correct by construction; date caps 366d + per_page ≤200 guard the DB).
- Per-user rate limiting on analytics endpoints deferred to Block 6 as planned.

## What changed
- **Charts**: `recharts@2.15` (why: React-18-native, composable Line/Bar/Area + tooltips, no cgo-like native deps, ~100KB; heatmap stays hand-rolled in Block 5).
- **New pages** (all under `AdminLayout`, all with loading/error/empty states, tooltips + text labels not color-only):
  - `/admin/analytics` — 6 KPI cards with prev-period deltas, presets (today/7d/30d/MTD/custom, EAT-labeled), stacked volume-area per currency (never summed), tx bars, success-rate line.
  - `/admin/analytics/providers` — tx-share bars, full table (volume, success, p50/p95 latency, 1h/24h failure signals, channel split, top failure badge).
  - `/admin/analytics/merchants` — tabs Top (sortable + CSV), Signup funnel (bars + conversion + median step hours), Dormant + Churn risk (reason, copy-contact-email, CSV). Rows link to `/admin/orgs/:orgId`.
  - `/admin/analytics/failures` — ranked reasons with EN + SW explanations and expandable sample order ids.
  - `/admin/ops` — stuck/unreconciled/negative/aging/webhook-health with count badges (red/amber), CSV buttons, **45s auto-refresh toggle**.
  - `/admin/orgs/:orgId` — operator org detail (profile, members, verification history). **Required a small backend addition**: `GET /api/v1/admin/orgs/:id` (the link target didn't exist).
- **Shared**: `analyticsApi.ts` client, `analyticsCommon.tsx` (presets, DeltaBadge, money/rate formatters, CSV button). Every table paginated server-side where applicable + CSV export button.
- **Nav**: Home·Analytics·Provider stats·Merchants·Failures·Ops·Payments·Apps·Withdrawals·Pay providers·KYC review.

# Phase 2 BLOCK 4 REPORT — done, committed (`fe649be`), pushed ✓

## What changed
7 org-scoped endpoints (membership + role resolved server-side; `app_id` validated against the org; 403 otherwise):
- `GET /orgs/:id/analytics/overview` (reuses platform Overview pinned to the org + avg order value), `/methods` (channel mix), `/peak-hours` (EAT weekday×hour grid + best/worst plain-language labels), `/customers` (repeat rate, new-vs-returning series, masked top payers), `/failures` (org-scoped breakdown), `/apps` (per-app comparison incl. idle apps).
- `GET /orgs/:id/settlements?format=json|csv|pdf` — **ledger-sourced** (gross/fees/refunds/net + opening/closing + per-provider + itemized, capped 5000 with truncation flag). PDF requires `?currency=` (one statement per currency).
- **Roles**: any active member reads; exports need owner/finance (`PermWithdraw` = owner+finance); **developers get aggregates with `payer_detail_hidden: true`** (no top-payer table).
- **Env toggle**: `?environment=live|sandbox`, live default; sandbox never mixes.
- **Exports**: 10/min per-user rate limit + audit-logged. PDF via `go-pdf/fpdf` (pure Go, no cgo — why: lightest maintained lib with tables/headers/page numbers; letterhead, per-currency blocks, itemized table, page X/of-Y).
- New dep: `github.com/go-pdf/fpdf v0.9.0`.

## Verified
- `go build/vet/test ./...` all pass.
- **Live**: all 7 endpoints OK; cross-org read → `403 forbidden`; customers endpoint fixed through 3 SQL iterations (placeholder numbering across builders — the `offset` field on `condBuilder` is the lasting fix).
- **Statement test passes on live postgres**: net `7800.00` and closing `6800.00` match independent ledger recomputation; CSV contains statement id; PDF starts `%PDF`.

# Phase 2 BLOCK 6 REPORT — done, committed (`7f30029`), pushed ✓

## What changed
- **Perf**: Overview now reads pre-aggregated rollups for whole EAT days + live tables for partial edges/today (with live fallback for missing days); new `first_paid_at` column (stamped in the paid-transition lock, backfilled from history) kills the history join; independent queries run concurrently; range indexes + TTP covering index (migrations `000047`–`000050`); 60s service TTL cache on Overview/TopMerchants.
- **Proof on 1M rows / 200 orgs** (dev laptop, noisy): overview ~650–1000ms cold / ~0ms warm; top ~0.7–1.8s cold / ~0ms warm; simple endpoints 200–500ms. Honest note in `docs/ANALYTICS.md`: the 500ms cold target isn't fully met on dev iron — warm p95 is ~0ms. Next levers documented.
- **Security**: per-user rate limit (60/min) on all analytics routes (auth runs first so 401s don't consume budget); range caps (366d, hour ≤ 7d) + `400` errors; exports already audited + rate-limited.
- **Tests**: HTTP-level isolation test (cross-org 403 on all 7 merchant endpoints, foreign app_id rejected, both audience directions 401) + Overview equivalence test (rollup == live fallback == hand truth) — both pass on live postgres. Privacy grep: raw phones only feed `mask()`, never serialized.
- **Seed tool**: `cmd/seed-analytics` (idempotent `analytics-seed-` prefix, payer HMAC matching Go normalization, history + ledger, `-bench` with timings + EXPLAIN).

## Untested
- `go test -race` (no gcc). Multi-process cache coherency: 60s TTL per process can serve slightly different numbers across api/worker — acceptable for dashboards, documented.

**Block 7** (docs reference, README nav, vitest + URL-synced filters) is next — continuing.

1: # LipaGO — frontend
2:
3: React panel for LipaGO: signup, organizations, apps, API keys, providers,
4: withdrawals, orders/ledger/events. It talks only to the Go backend via
5: `VITE_API_BASE_URL`.

7: ## Setup
8:
9: ```
10: cp .env.example .env
11: # VITE_API_BASE_URL — where you deployed backend/ (defaults to http://localhost:8080 in dev)
12:
13: npm install
14: npm run dev
15: ```
16:

18: npm run build      # production build → dist/
19: npm run preview    # preview the production build locally
20: ```
21:
22: ## Signing in
23:
24: 1. Create the first admin on the backend with
25:    `go run ./cmd/seed-admin -email you@example.com` (self-registration
26:    never grants admin).
27: 2. Sign in at `/signin` — you land in the admin panel with full access:
28:    create payment apps, generate API keys, configure providers, review
29:    orders/ledger, approve or reject withdrawals.
30: 3. Merchants sign up at `/signup` (email + OTP verification), create an
31:    organization at `/onboarding/create-org`, and can work in sandbox mode
32:    immediately. Live API keys/payments unlock after the org's verification
33:    is submitted at `/onboarding/kyc/:orgId` and approved.
34:
35: ## Pages
36:
37: | Route | Purpose |
38: |---|---|
39: | `/signup` | merchant signup + email OTP verification |
40: | `/admin/payments` | overview / metrics |

42: | `/admin/payments/apps/:id` | single app detail — orders, ledger, webhook endpoints |
43: | `/admin/payments/withdrawals` | review and act on withdrawal requests |
44: | `/admin/payments/providers` | configure payment provider credentials |
45: | `/admin/kyc` | verification review queue (approve/reject, per-org live limits) |
46: | `/merchant/apps` | merchant app list (org-scoped) + self-service app creation |
47: | `/merchant/apps/:id` | app detail — rename, webhooks, labeled API keys, deliveries |
48: | `/onboarding/create-org` | create an organization |
49: | `/onboarding/kyc/:orgId` | verification submission (business name, TIN, ID doc) |
50: | `/org/:orgId/members` | member roles & invites |
51: | `/org/:orgId/settings` | org settings + verification status |
52:
53: Unverified orgs show a sandbox-mode banner (live keys/payments blocked).
54:

256: ## API surface
257:
258: - `POST /api/v1/payments/orders` — create a payment order (public, app-API-key auth)
259: - `GET /api/v1/payments/orders/{paymentID}` — order status (public, auto-refreshes stale orders)
260: - `POST /api/v1/payments/orders/{paymentID}/refresh` — force a live provider status check (public, app-API-key auth)
261: - `POST /api/v1/payments/webhooks/{provider}` — inbound provider webhooks (public)
262: - `POST /api/v1/admin/payments/orders/{id}/refund` — refund a paid order (admin-auth).
263:   Optional JSON body `{amount?, currency?, reason?}`; omitted amount refunds
264:   the full remaining amount. Currency must match the order; amounts above the
265:   remaining refundable total are rejected (422 `amount_exceeded`). Response
266:   `{data: {order, refund}}`. Every attempt is recorded in
267:   `app.payment_refunds` (order, provider refund id, amount, status, reason).
268: - `/api/v1/admin/payments/...` — apps, providers, orders, events,
269:   deliveries, withdrawals, metrics (admin-auth)
270: - `/api/v1/merchant/apps/...` — merchant-facing views for app members
271: - `/api/v1/merchant/apps/{id}/webhook-endpoints` — merchant webhook CRUD
272:   (GET/POST), plus `PATCH`/`DELETE .../{endpointID}` and
273:   `POST .../{endpointID}/test-send` (signed live probe, nothing stored)
274: - `/api/v1/merchant/apps/{id}/api-keys` — list (prefixes only) + create;
275:   `POST .../{keyID}/rotate` (old keys stay valid 24h) and
276:   `POST .../{keyID}/revoke` (immediate)
277: - `GET /api/v1/merchant/apps/{id}/deliveries` — delivery logs scoped to
278:   the app, plus `POST .../{deliveryID}/replay`
279: - All merchant routes require a signed-in session AND app membership —
280:   the app id always comes from the verified path, never client input.
281: - `GET /api/v1/health` — liveness + DB check
282: - `GET /api/v1/admin/me` — `{email, is_admin}` for the signed-in user
283:
284: Merchant webhook event types: `payment.updated`, `payment.refunded`
285: (emitted after every confirmed refund, same signing as other events),
286: `payment.expired` (emitted when a pending order passes its TTL).
287: New endpoints subscribe to all three by default.
